emails.subject: Meet Up
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Just want to thank you for the Christmas card. Very kind of you.

I hope you’re well and we must meet up again in the New Year. I am working on a football shift tomorrow so will let the guys know you’re keen and available.

All the best for Christmas and New Year.

Nick

P.S. I’m not so sure we will sack Levien after all!!! 4-0 !!

From: Jamie Murray []
Sent: 14 November 2017 13:49
To: Nicholas Walker
Importance: High

Hello Nicholas,

My name is Jamie Murray and I study Television Production at City of Glasgow Collage. I was in the class the day you came along to give us a talk about the work you do at STV. I was very impressed with your promo for the national team. It certainly captured the excitement felt by fans in the run up to facing England. In particular, 35 seconds into the Scotland v England promo there is a beautifully edited section as the presenter says: “as for the players lucky enough to pull on the jersey”. I would love to see how you managed to achieve that.

I wanted to email you because I will be at STV for a runners placement on Live at 5 from Wednesday 15th to Wednesday 22nd of November. I will also be in for my studio placement from Monday 27th to Friday 1st of December.

I was wondering if there was any chance you would have time to meet me in person either on one of those days before my placement times begin to discuss in more depth the work you do for STV. I am very interested in sport myself and as I study TV, and aim to work in the industry I feel I would greatly benefit from seeing the kind of things you are tasked with and the content you are working on.

Do you think something like that would be possible? I understand you must be very busy but I’d really like to meet with you again.

I have attached my CV for further reference into my skills and experience so far in the industry.

P.s I noticed you are a Hearts fan. That’s also something I think would spark some interesting conversation!!!!

I eagerly await your response.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

emails.subject: Opportunities with STV2
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Many thanks for getting in touch – and many apologies for the inordinate delay in getting back to you.

As you surmise, we have several productions in the final stages of the delivery process and life has been more than manic in recent days!

As you also surmise, once these programmes are delivered we are all going off on a two week break – so things really are winding down.

I’d love you to get in touch in the new year. We can always use some help with our VT and studio productions, and I believe ‘hands on’ experience can be invaluable to ambitious students like yourself. You would be more than welcome to do some shadowing and get the opportunity to pick the brains of the people who work here.

Let me know if there are any particular areas you’d like some experience in, and I am sure we can get something set up in January or whenever suits.

‘Look forward to hearing from you.

Merry Christmas when it comes.

Regards,

Angus

Angus Simpson | Programme Producer STV2 | Tel: 0141 300 3290 | Mob: 07818 023623
email: [email removed] | website: www.stv.tv
STV | Pacific Quay | Glasgow | G51 1PQ | switchboard: 0141 300 3000
Please consider the environment before printing this email

From: Jamie Murray []
Sent: 10 December 2017 23:38
To: Angus Simpson
Importance: High

Hello Angus,

I met you last year when I was doing my gallery placement on Live At FIve when you were producing some of the shows.

I’ve since been back in STV these past few weeks working under Hollie Anderson in my runners placement and again the week after working under Innis Strachan and Mark McClymont completing my studio placement. I have found both placements very enjoyable and incredibly worthwhile.

I am a HND TV student at City of Glasgow College in my second year and I have applied to University to take my television production studies further.

I know that you produce a large amount of the content for STV. Hollie had mentioned you were travelling around Scotland shooting for the Christmas Choir show.

I was wondering if there was any scope for someone like myself, looking to gain more experience in production and eager to learn more and help out in any capacity to perhaps get involved with some of the things you are working on?

I wondered if perhaps there would be any opportunities for me to help out on any of the other shoots you are working on or if there was a chance some of the freelancers that produce the VTs used on Live At Five needed an extra pair of hands? I had mentioned to one of STV2 Technical Operators, Mark McClymont whilst on placement, that the VT for when the presenter David was picking the Christmas Tree for the studio was particularly well produced and featured some absolutely beautiful shots.

I realise that things may be winding down for this year so if you think that maybe there is more opportunities for this sort of thing I could get back in contact with you early next year and we could possibly arrange something?

I hope you have received my email well and I look forward to hearing back from you.

I have attached my CV for further reference into my skills and experience I’ve gained so far.

Have a wonderful Christmas and New Years if I don’t hear from you before then.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

From: Jamie Murray []

Importance: High

Hello Bryan,

My name is Jamie Murray. I am a Television student at City of Glasgow Collage in the second year of my HND.

I finished my floor runners placement with Live at Five working under Hollie Anderson on Wednesday. Initially after speaking to her about the football show you work on at STV, she advised that I ought to get in contact with you abut it.

I wanted to email you because I will be at STV for a studio placement on Live at 5 from Monday 27th to Friday 1st of December and I was wondering if there was any chance you would have time to meet me in person either on one of those days before my placement times begin to discuss in more depth the work you do for STV.

I am very interested in sport myself and as I study TV, and aim to work in the industry I feel I would greatly benefit from seeing the kind of things you are tasked with and the content you are working on. I am trying to immerse myself within the industry to gain as much as experience as I can and wondered if there would be any scope for me to get involved in the production of Peter & Roughie's Football Show? I am willing to help out in any capacity whatsoever if you feel that is something that is possible.

I understand you must be very busy but I’d really like to meet with you.

I have attached my CV for further reference into my skills and experience so far in the industry.

I eagerly await your response.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Thank you very much for your feedback on my Scotland promo.

That’s great to hear that you’re getting in the door here and working in a live studio environment. I walk past the Live at 5 studio everyday to go to my sound dubbing sessions.

Tomorrow we are filming THE LATE SHOW at 1100 - bit earlier than usual and looking for audience members to come in.

Let me know if you can make it in and if you would like to bring anyone along.

Best,
Hollie

emails.subject: BBC - Production Trainee Scheme - Careers
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Apologies I’ve not been in touch sooner - it’s been a really hectic time leading up to Christmas. This is the scheme that I joined the BBC with 8 years ago, and I think it would be a great idea for you to apply. Applications are open now, so get one in as soon as you can - it’s hugely oversubscribed so make it a good one! Happy to give you any help or advice if you feel you need it.

Hope you’ve had a fabo Christmas! 

All the best,

Rowan 

Sent from my iPhone

Hi Jamie,

Thank you very much. I had a great day thanks.

Looking forward to hearing from you soon.

Kind regards,

Jamie

emails.subject: UWS Perspective Student - RangersTV
emails.body:
Hello Jamie,

Sorry for the delay in replying, been a busy week. Wednesday night looked great, need to get a good run going now! On a matchday I mostly deal with Go Pros and Super Slo Motion footage using an FS700. They go into wee videos like this which I filmed and edited. Calum provided me with the real time footage.

I film the odd post match interview too which is good fun also.

As for being in Glasgow, obviously the travel to and from Ayr is a factor. I'm from Glasgow and was travelling from Kings Park everyday. For me it was well worth it though. I'm obviously biased but I enjoyed it. The train journey was a chance to read or sleep anyway! If you're living in Glasgow then it's the same difference for you getting work experience so I wouldn't worry about that. The only thing to consider is the travel to Ayr as far as I'm concerned, without knowing what other offers you have then I can say for definite that you'd enjoy coming to UWS. We've got good facilities, good equipment, great staff and hopefully good contacts with the industry. And as I mentioned there's an emphasis on combining practical ability and creative thinking with academic thinking and writing. The course has been great for me, a real life changer, everyone's circumstances are different of course but I'm really glad I studied here.

I think Nick was in my year, I didn't know him too well but yeah he's done really well.

Hope that answers your questions. Any more let me know. Lets keep in touch and we'll clarify the Hearts game nearer the time.

Cheers

Jamie

Jamie Hare

Room 2.001

UWS Ayr Campus

University Avenue

Ayr

KA8 0SX

01292 886 463

________________________________
From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: 23 January 2018 13:11:03
To: Jamie Hare

Hello again Jamie,

It's great to hear back from you so soon!

That is amazing that you have the chance to work most match days at Ibrox. You much relish the opportunity! It would be absolutely brilliant to attend a home game with you and I would really appreciate the chance to see what you get up to throughout the fixture. I am actually going to the game tomorrow night against Aberdeen, really looking forward to the second part of the league - we have definitely strengthened in this window. Hearts on the 24th would be perfect for me, thank you so much. Can I ask what your duties are? Are you there princably as a photographer, videographer or do you perhaps help out in various capacities?

Following my interview with Paul I received an offer for UWS which was great. As I mentioned before, I am currently studying at City of Glasgow College where there is an option to progress onto the degree course for TV, if you apply and get in. I thought being in Glasgow may be more practical in terms of finding work experience and opportunities working within the industry, what are you thoughts on this? It is great to hear that Paul has been such a positive force in your career so far. You can't ask for much more from a lecturer which is really pleasing to hear - having only met him once, he has already provided me access to an amazing opportunity. Also, it is great to hear more of the staff at UWS are also as helpful as Paul.

Studying a course that is respected by employers is vital I think. I've met Nick Walker, who works as a promo editor at STV, and I am sure he is a graduate of BP at UWS and he certainly benefited from his time there from what he has told me. I am hopefully going back to STV to shadow some Video Journalist who create the VTs for Live At Five etc on STV2 and hopefully to meet Nick again. It's interesting to see where people choose to study. The balance between practical and critical writing is important to me also as I would like to strengthen my skills theoretically as well as practically, and it seems you would highly recommend UWS for that?

I'd love to come along to the Hearts game with you. It would a brilliant experience to meet with yourself and some of the others who work in the team. Exiting game also with those two making a return to Ibrox, hopefully they don't celebrate too much if they score like Chris Burke did!!

Looking forward to hearing from you and thanks once again.

Kind regards,
Jamie

On Monday, 22 January 2018, 23:36, Jamie Hare wrote:

Hello Jamie,

Thanks for your email. Paul did mentioned he'd spoken to you.

Firstly Rangers, like you I've been a big fan all my life and I work most match days with the TV guys which as you can imagine is great. I've been taking students along with me and as you know Andy and Calum are working full time there now and obviously enjoying it. I'm sure I could get you with me for a home game to see what the guys do. I'm actually missing the game on Wednesday and I've promised someone else I'll take them to Hibs on the 3rd of February. We could provisionally pencil in Hearts on the 24th if that suits you?

Secondly if you've been offered a place on the Broadcast Production I'd definitely take it. I really enjoyed it, both for the practical work I was able to do and the critical thinking about television I did which enabled me to go to interviews for jobs fully prepared to discuss what I liked and didn't like about TV with people who had been making it for several years, which was vital in me getting a job shortly after graduating. Almost as important were the contacts I made, probably none more so than Paul himself. He got me my first work experience (with him directing), my first paid work and got me in touch with the person that gave me my first job. And there's plenty more people like him around.

We've got a lot of BP graduates in sport now. In recent years we've had graduates at Glasgow Warriors, Celtic TV, SPFL, SFA, SRU and of course Rangers so the course is well respected by potential employers. In addition there's plenty of people working in other areas, drama, game shows, Ob-Docs, various factual formats so our graduates are getting opportunities once they've left us.

Anyway let me know what you think about the Hearts game, be an interesting day with Naismith and Lafferty at Ibrox, hopefully we can build on the mostly good results before the break and get a good run going again! Happy to talk more about the course then or if you've any questions about what I've been doing then fire away.

Cheers mate,

Jamie

From: Jamie Murray

To: Jamie Hare

Good afternoon Jamie,

My name is Jamie Murray and I am a student at City of Glasgow College studying Television Production. I was advised to contact you by Paul Tucker, senior lecturer at UWS following my interview for the Broadcast Production degree course. I had brought up in conversation my recent attempts to gain some work experience with RangersTV by finding some emails on the club website but I couldn’t find the approbate people. I also mentioned that I had found Andy Jess and Calum Walker on social media who were prolific in showing their following the wonderful job they do as part of the media team at Rangers.

Paul mentioned he had spoken with you and advised me to contact you regarding the possibility of a ‘trail shift’ where I could meet Andy and Calum. I also wondered what your experience of the Broadcast Production course at UWS was and if you’d recommend it?

In terms of the experience I have already gained in TV production, I have had placements at STV's Live at Five show for a combined period of three weeks. Last June, I completed a work placement at Pinewood TV in London, I transcribed for Scrumptious Productions for three days last September and in October, I was part of a crew that filmed Sir Alex Ferguson in a one-to-one interview for the Nelson Mandela Memorial Campaign. I would really love to get some experience in sport broadcasting and even more so at Rangers, a team I have passionately supported through-out my life!

I have attached my CV for further reference into my skills and experience.

I eagerly await your response and thank you for taking your time to read my email.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

emails.subject: Opportunities with STV2
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

‘Happy New Year!

Thanks for getting in touch again. Although, we are now into the new year, I’m afraid we are still waiting to hear of programme plans for 2018. We have a new management team who are putting things together as we speak.

I have checked with Angela, our Production Manager, and we are ‘full up’ with Live at Five runners for the next few weeks – but then I think you have ‘been there and done that’.

Let me see if I can get you to shadow one of our VJs for a couple of days towards the end of the month. Let me know your availability and we will see what we can do.

‘See you soon,

Angus

From: Jamie Murray []
Sent: 15 January 2018 07:22
To: Angus Simpson

Hello again Angus,

I hope you had a wonderful time over the festive period.

I thought I would write you again in a little follow up email, as we are now half way through January, to see if there may any opportunities coming up where I could get some experience with you and your production team at STV.

As previously mentioned, I’d love to help out the production teams and guys who make the VTs for Live at Five (or 7.30!).

Additionally, if there are any upcoming shoots where you may need any runners or someone to help out the production team in any capacity I’d love to do that as well.

I look forward to any opportunities and to hearing back from you.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

On 14 Dec 2017, at 11:59, Angus Simpson > wrote:

Hi Jamie,

Many thanks for getting in touch – and many apologies for the inordinate delay in getting back to you.

As you surmise, we have several productions in the final stages of the delivery process and life has been more than manic in recent days!

As you also surmise, once these programmes are delivered we are all going off on a two week break – so things really are winding down.

I’d love you to get in touch in the new year. We can always use some help with our VT and studio productions, and I believe ‘hands on’ experience can be invaluable to ambitious students like yourself. You would be more than welcome to do some shadowing and get the opportunity to pick the brains of the people who work here.

Let me know if there are any particular areas you’d like some experience in, and I am sure we can get something set up in January or whenever suits.

‘Look forward to hearing from you.

Merry Christmas when it comes.

Regards,

Angus

Thanks for the email. It was a pleasure to meet you and I hope that you choose to come to UWS - it would be good to have you here.

I remember that you brought up The Crown in the group discussion. You may be interested in this https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2018/jan/20/clive-james-on-the-crown-queen-joe-shmuck

'She is the Queen, whereas you are Joe Shmuck': Clive James on The Crown
www.theguardian.com
How to recover from my latest hospital stay? Watch The Crown – twice, and remember a royal meeting of my own

Clive James invented modern TV criticism in the 70s and 80s as well as having a prolific TV and writing career. I was lucky enough to work with him in the early 90s.

As far as Rangers go, the best first contact would be Jamie Hare - [email removed]. He is a graduate of the Broadcast Production TV and Radio course and really where the link with Rangers started. I've spoken to him about you and, if you email him, he should be able to arrange a trial 'shift' at Rangers. You'll then be able to meet Callum and Andy.

Let me know how it goes.

Best

Paul

emails.subject: UWS Perspective Student - RangersTV
emails.body:
Good afternoon Jamie,

My name is Jamie Murray and I am a student at City of Glasgow College studying Television Production. I was advised to contact you by Paul Tucker, senior lecturer at UWS following my interview for the Broadcast Production degree course. I had brought up in conversation my recent attempts to gain some work experience with RangersTV by finding some emails on the club website but I couldn’t find the approbate people. I also mentioned that I had found Andy Jess and Calum Walker on social media who were prolific in showing their following the wonderful job they do as part of the media team at Rangers.

Paul mentioned he had spoken with you and advised me to contact you regarding the possibility of a ‘trail shift’ where I could meet Andy and Calum. I also wondered what your experience of the Broadcast Production course at UWS was and if you’d recommend it?

In terms of the experience I have already gained in TV production, I have had placements at STV's Live at Five show for a combined period of three weeks. Last June, I completed a work placement at Pinewood TV in London, I transcribed for Scrumptious Productions for three days last September and in October, I was part of a crew that filmed Sir Alex Ferguson in a one-to-one interview for the Nelson Mandela Memorial Campaign. I would really love to get some experience in sport broadcasting and even more so at Rangers, a team I have passionately supported through-out my life! 

I have attached my CV for further reference into my skills and experience.

I eagerly await your response and thank you for taking your time to read my email.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

emails.subject: UWS Perspective Student - RangersTV
emails.body:
Hello Jamie,

Thanks for your email. Paul did mentioned he'd spoken to you.

Firstly Rangers, like you I've been a big fan all my life and I work most match days with the TV guys which as you can imagine is great. I've been taking students along with me and as you know Andy and Calum are working full time there now and obviously enjoying it. I'm sure I could get you with me for a home game to see what the guys do. I'm actually missing the game on Wednesday and I've promised someone else I'll take them to Hibs on the 3rd of February. We could provisionally pencil in Hearts on the 24th if that suits you?

Secondly if you've been offered a place on the Broadcast Production I'd definitely take it. I really enjoyed it, both for the practical work I was able to do and the critical thinking about television I did which enabled me to go to interviews for jobs fully prepared to discuss what I liked and didn't like about TV with people who had been making it for several years, which was vital in me getting a job shortly after graduating. Almost as important were the contacts I made, probably none more so than Paul himself. He got me my first work experience (with him directing), my first paid work and got me in touch with the person that gave me my first job. And there's plenty more people like him around.

We've got a lot of BP graduates in sport now. In recent years we've had graduates at Glasgow Warriors, Celtic TV, SPFL, SFA, SRU and of course Rangers so the course is well respected by potential employers. In addition there's plenty of people working in other areas, drama, game shows, Ob-Docs, various factual formats so our graduates are getting opportunities once they've left us.

Anyway let me know what you think about the Hearts game, be an interesting day with Naismith and Lafferty at Ibrox, hopefully we can build on the mostly good results before the break and get a good run going again! Happy to talk more about the course then or if you've any questions about what I've been doing then fire away.

Cheers mate,

Jamie

emails.subject: UWS Perspective Student - RangersTV Good afternoon Jamie,
emails.body:
Hello again Jamie,
It's great to hear back from you so soon! 
That is amazing that you have the chance to work most match days at Ibrox. You much relish the opportunity! It would be absolutely brilliant to attend a home game with you and I would really appreciate the chance to see what you get up to throughout the fixture. I am actually going to the game tomorrow night against Aberdeen, really looking forward to the second part of the league - we have definitely strengthened in this window. Hearts on the 24th would be perfect for me, thank you so much. Can I ask what your duties are? Are you there princably as a photographer, videographer or do you perhaps help out in various capacities?
Following my interview with Paul I received an offer for UWS which was great. As I mentioned before, I am currently studying at City of Glasgow College where there is an option to progress onto the degree course for TV, if you apply and get in. I thought being in Glasgow may be more practical in terms of finding work experience and opportunities working within the industry, what are you thoughts on this? It is great to hear that Paul has been such a positive force in your career so far. You can't ask for much more from a lecturer which is really pleasing to hear - having only met him once, he has already provided me access to an amazing opportunity. Also, it is great to hear more of the staff at UWS are also as helpful as Paul.
Studying a course that is respected by employers is vital I think. I've met Nick Walker, who works as a promo editor at STV, and I am sure he is a graduate of BP at UWS and he certainly benefited from his time there from what he has told me. I am hopefully going back to STV to shadow some Video Journalist who create the VTs for Live At Five etc on STV2 and hopefully to meet Nick again. It's interesting to see where people choose to study. The balance between practical and critical writing is important to me also as I would like to strengthen my skills theoretically as well as practically, and it seems you would highly recommend UWS for that?
I'd love to come along to the Hearts game with you. It would a brilliant experience to meet with yourself and some of the others who work in the team. Exiting game also with those two making a return to Ibrox, hopefully they don't celebrate too much if they score like Chris Burke did!!
Looking forward to hearing from you and thanks once again.
Kind regards,Jamie

emails.subject: NEW YEAR NEW ME
emails.body:
Hello The Social Contributors!

LAST CALL FOR IDEAS FOR 2019
If you have any incoming ideas that are for December, we absolutley need it by Tuesday (17th) as next week is the last week we’re in the office. I’ll be out of office from Monday 23rd Dec until Jan 6th, any emails in between then will get picked up when I’m back. If you’ve just thought of the absolute best idea ever for xmas, save it for next year and get some January ideas on the go!

PAPERWORK
I’ve attached a quick reminder for paperwork, please read it and keep it as a quick reference for future. Not complying with it can really stuff things up for your video, and worst case scenario make it un-useable. Getting good at it will set you up well for working in other parts of the media.

NEW IDEAS AND YOUR CAREER
The Social should be a place for new creative ideas to get made about things you’re passionate about, but don’t pigeonhole yourself, I’m keen to hear all sorts of ideas that reflect your interests but also help reflect modern Scotland. The new BBC Scotland channel is an amazing opportunity for people who make content for The Social to develop ideas for. If you have formats or ideas you think might work in other mediums such as tv or podcasts or longer youtube strands, then let me know, but just remember getting to TV can be a long process so the key is to always be working towards that. The more you tell me about your career ambitions the easier it is for me to help you navigate the BBC and the wider media landscape.

THANKS
Thanks for everything this year (I know it’s not over yet!), the continued work and effort you all put into making videos is what makes The Social work. It’s been brilliant to work with so many of you throughout the year and looking forward to starting up again in January!

If you’ve just recently got involved, start sending over ideas and let’s get going. If you’ve not had time to be involved recently, the beginning of the year is a great time to start up again and get fired up.
Look forward to catching up with you in the new year.

Cheers

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

My class has finished if you want to come to 06.081 whenever suits.

Lorna
________________________________
From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: 03 December 2019 11:22
To: Lorna Donnet 

Hello Lorna,

Last thing on the log, could you take a look at this paragraph, to make sure it makes sense!

I supported Thomas in sourcing the presenter for Prize Draw by utilising his connections with BBC The Social contributors. In professional practice, they would have casting directors and liaise with agents when sourcing contributors but as a student production, we couldn’t afford such luxuries. I wanted to give other students an opportunity to be in a proper production when recruiting for our production, so I met with acting student, Alexander, who agreed to take part in Prize Draw and secure the help of his fellow classmates. As production neared, Alexander stopped communicating with me, which then put me under a significant time restraint to find four contributors. This experience was mirrored with Thomas, who was also let down last minute. As Decker and Austin convey in Peculiar Portrayals (2010), narrative television requires relatable contestants. However, given severe time constraints, we were forced to accept those who responded to our casting call. In future, I wouldn’t reply solely on one person saying yes. I became frustrated with the limitations of our student production. It would be unlikely for a professional production to have contributors pull out, but because we were a student production I felt people didn’t take it seriously. I wish I had started sourcing contributors the day I met with Alexander, as I then wasted four days trying to get a response from him with no success.

I think Thursday may be a stretch given the size of this assessment, so will we go for Friday?

Kind regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Filming about accessible toilets
emails.body:
Hey Jamie,

No worries at all – does the 10th or 11th work for you?

I usually use a Gh4 [lenses, I have 12mm, 25mm, 35-100mm] and rode radio mics. I don’t have a shoulder rig right now or LED portable light, so that’s the only thing, but I got everything else. I’m happy to bring my kit, whatever works best!

London was all work! So I’m completely knackered...got one more presentation tomorrow and then I can sleep and be a functional human being!

Kindest regards,
Kiana
Sent from Mail for Windows 10

emails.subject: Video pick ups
emails.body:
Hi both,

Thanks for the first draft of the video, it’s nicely put together but it was really missing those themes around employability to help frame your story and also the parts about the success you’ve had in your career.
I’ve attached the script, since it can be challenging to try and memorise lots of text and deliver it to camera, I’m happy for you to work off bullet points, however it’s really important that you have the script to hand too so that you can review clips and make sure it’s still covering the key points and there’s continuity throughout.

I like this idea of you talking about a bigger issue of employability for disabled people and using your own story and also success to help change attitudes. I think that’s a much stronger idea than telling your story and will really resonate with people.

Hope that all makes sense!

I’ll let you two see if there’s a time that suits to film and we can take it from there.

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

emails.subject: Postponement
emails.body: Hi, We have decided that this week isn't the best time to host the pitching to a commissioner session. Muslim Alim is very busy and we would like to really make the most of the opportunity of having him in to speak, meet students and give feedback on pitches. The numbers available attend on Thursday are very low due to work experience placements, assessment deadlines and personal circumstances. Therefore we are postponing this event until mid January. We would very much like everyone to think about and prep a property show idea over the festive season. So Thursday is self study all day or if anyone wishes to show draft work to Andrew or myself we are available for one to ones - send us an email. Best wishes, Kate

emails.subject: Details for Tomorrow - The Social Contributor Christmas Gathering -
emails.body:
Hi everyone!

We can't wait to see you all at the annual The Social Contributor Christmas Gathering tomorrow, 19:30-22:30 at BBC Scotland, Glasgow!

There are a couple of things to highlight before the event.

* Please remember to take ID with you. There will be security and they may request to see it.

* No plus ones are allowed, only those on the guest list will be admitted.

* Members of the team will be escorting guests through to the event, as all external guests must be with a member of staff at all times. The party will be in the Ancillary Building, which is at the back of the main BBC Scotland building.

* There are toilets in the Ancillary Building.

* If you need to leave the building, please let one of the team know and they will escort you out.

* Be mindful that The Nine and The Edit broadcast live in the main building from 21:00, so if you are in the main foyer after this time, please be as quiet as possible.

If you have any questions or queries, please don't hesitate to get in touch :)

See you all tomorrow!

Sam

Samantha Little
Production Management Assistant
BBC The Social

emails.body:

Job: Sports Videographer at Youth Football Scotland in Glasgow, Glasgow
Name: Jamie Murray
Email: [email removed]
CV: Jamie Murray CV.pdf
Message:

Dear Youth Football Scotland,

My name is Jamie Murray and I have worked in Scotland’s television production industry, across a number of sporting projects over the last two years. I believe the skills I have acquired during this time, as a videographer make me the perfect candidate for this freelance role with YFS.

Last Summer I worked as a camera assistant on PurpleTV’s BBC Alba feature-length documentary ‘Tommy Burns’. I was recruited for this role by Gavin Hopkins, a Glasgow-based camera operator and I assisted him on an interview shoot with Kenny Dalglish in Liverpool. Also during the ‘Tommy Burns’ project, I also assisted Gavin at Hampden Park, Celtic Park, Maryhill FC's ground and Kilmarnock FC's Rugby Park. Previously I have also filmed a promotional video for semi-professional club Newmains United, shot an interview with Sir Alex Ferguson in Glasgow City Chambers in 2016 and had experience filming pitch-side with Rangers TV last year.

Earlier this year, I accompanied DOP Keith Ingram to Ayr beach where we shot a football promo for the BBC which featured Biffy Clyro’s Simon Neil as the presenter. It was a great experience filming with recognised talent.

In addition to filming sport I recently shot a video for the Scottish Social Services Awards which examined the topic of homelessness in Scotland (https://vimeo.com/339535235). I was also recently one of the winners of the Scottish Parliament One Minute Film Competition where I shot a video about a Syrian refugee named Mounzar, who has made Scotland his new home (https://youtu.be/ru_LITxyt5M). Various other examples of my work can be found here: https://www.jamieamurray.com/projects. 

I have attached my CV and a more detailed covering letter (PDF) for your consideration.

Kit List: Sony A7III, Tripod, Rode Video Mic Pro + Radio Mics, I edit on Premiere Pro with my Macbook Pro and I have a driving licence with my own car.

Showreel: https://www.jamieamurray.com/showreel

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray

emails.subject: Evaluation Log
emails.body:
Hi,

That looks OK - and understood, there's a lot more than 1500 words can cover and it's difficult to nail everything.

A producer's role is so important. Have you reflected on the casting and directing of talent? A crucially important part of the development and recording.

I will be most impressed by your reflection if you're able to identify where you, personally, could have done better. I'm not interested in calling you out on anything that didn't go well but I am interested in what you learned about your own performance - LO3, enhanced production skills in specialist role and LO4 develop personal and production management and communication skills.

A reflection allows you the opportunity to identify what you could have done better and make clear the learning in the process undertaken. Leadership isn't easy. Hats off to those who take on that role with humility and respect for those they lead.

We often underestimate how hard it is to make programmes that are so easy to watch.

Hope this helps. In 6.48 and able to talk on mobile number below if that would help.

James

James Wilson
Curriculum Head: Broadcasting
0141 375 8311 & 07899 761167
City of Glasgow College
City Campus
190 Cathedral Street
Glasgow
G4 0RF

Our TV students' work: https://vimeo.com/tvcityofglasgow

Hi James,

Okay, could I send your through the structure I have went with. Wondered if you could point me in any direction that you think I may not have covered.

I have written about:

Week 6: being assigned to a team, fulfilling my role, experiences of AES event working with Jim Hunter + masterclass with Des O’Hare. I have reflected on these things and how they helped with my preparation of production.

Week 7: Pitching to Gavin Smith, discussed professional studio examples such as Win, Lose or Draw and The Last Leg and how they inspired our production.

Week 8 + 9: (Pre-production) Discussed my experience of being a producer and my role with leading a large team, went into detail about the paperwork/preparations I completed for production, talked about getting contributors, the problems we faced and how that relates to professional practice.

Week 10: (Production) Adapting to problems with presenter and reflected on decisions I took to enhance the production despite the setbacks.

Week 11: Reflecting on the positives and shortcomings on Prize Draw. Looking at the production in the context of a student project vs professional environment and how that differs.

Conclusion:

Is there anything glaring out to you I should cover? It has been a struggle with only having 1500 words to work with. I have tried to remain dense in my descriptions and reflections and have included many textbook/academic references.

Look forward to hearing from you.

Really appreciate your help, I want to try and achieve the best mark possible.

Kind regards,
Jamie

From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: 03 December 2019 11:22
To: Lorna Donnet 

Hello Lorna,

Last thing on the log, could you take a look at this paragraph, to make sure it makes sense!

I supported Thomas in sourcing the presenter for Prize Draw by utilising his connections with BBC The Social contributors. In professional practice, they would have casting directors and liaise with agents when sourcing contributors but as a student production, we couldn’t afford such luxuries. I wanted to give other students an opportunity to be in a proper production when recruiting for our production, so I met with acting student, Alexander, who agreed to take part in Prize Draw and secure the help of his fellow classmates. As production neared, Alexander stopped communicating with me, which then put me under a significant time restraint to find four contributors. This experience was mirrored with Thomas, who was also let down last minute. As Decker and Austin convey in Peculiar Portrayals (2010), narrative television requires relatable contestants. However, given severe time constraints, we were forced to accept those who responded to our casting call. In future, I wouldn’t reply solely on one person saying yes. I became frustrated with the limitations of our student production. It would be unlikely for a professional production to have contributors pull out, but because we were a student production I felt people didn’t take it seriously. I wish I had started sourcing contributors the day I met with Alexander, as I then wasted four days trying to get a response from him with no success.

I think Thursday may be a stretch given the size of this assessment, so will we go for Friday?

Kind regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Re: 2 Videos
emails.body:
Hey Jamie!

Thanks for sending these over and hope you have a good new year eve!
Thanks again for going out to re-film with Michael, it’s a nice video and it’s come out really well, it’s been a bit challenging to get it to this stage and really appreciate you taking the time to do extra work on it.

Michael’s Vid
This is working a million times more, got a couple of questions then next steps for it.

 * 00:28 do you have shots of him talking to camera here?
 * 01:22 – 01:29 I think we can cut this and come it at “the doctors"

There’s quite a long section where he talks about his past and going on to Scotland tonight and The Nine.
Since I’ll get those clips and pass onto the researcher, I think the easiest thing to do is if you can upload a version with no cutaways on it, that will give us room to make a few snips and overlay the other footage. I think that makes more sense than getting you to make more changes when we don’t have those clips yet. If that makes sense!

So next step:

 * If you can adjust those couple of points above
 * Can you upload that version to dropbox
 * Upload clean version with no b-roll, if there are parts where he was reading off the script on camera, just leave the b roll on it and I’ll understand what’s going on
 * Can you upload the original version too? There are some audio parts that could also work in this and good to have an option
 * Deliverable forms plus the trancript.

Kiana’s vid
This is great, Kiana’s excellent on screen and really happy with all the technical aspects of filming and sound quality :)
Got a couple of queries and notes:

 * 00:28 think we could come back to a shot of Kiana at this point as it’s all b roll till 00:37
 * 01:02 any chance you have a cutaway of the footplates?
 * 01:04 this is a cool shot! Might work better to move it to 00:51? Although that might make it odd that she sort of then just appears in the toilet. Maybe if we lean into it and have a pop sfx it could work? What do you think?
 * 02:05 great shot!
 * I’m going to reach out to the changing places organisation for some media to see if there’s anything we can overlay that will help show what a CP toilet looks like
 * Can you take off the fade at the end?

Let me know what you think!
If you can make those changes where possible then next step is to get the deliverable form, transcript and then upload it with the video to your dropbox folder.

How’s your availability for the next few months? No doubt there will be projects you can get stuck into, and if you have other ideas you want to bring and pitch to make then just let me know!

Cheers!

emails.subject: BBC The Social - Filming Spoken Word Workshop
emails.body:
Good morning Jamie,

You are invited to our "Filming Spoken Word" workshop on Thursday the 23rd of January at BBC Scotland Pacific Quay, in Glasgow, hosted by Emily Brown, from The Social who is also a filmmaker with lots of experience in filming Spoken Word.

Spoken Word on The Social has become incredibly popular and is in constant demand. We have lots of Spoken Word artists, however we're lacking in Spoken Word filmmakers! The aim of the workshop is to bring filmmakers from The Social together, to network and learn some tips about filming Spoken Word.

Many filmmakers don't feel confident in filming Spoken Word as they may not have a poetry background, however there is no need! It's all about understanding storytelling, and it's a great opportunity to get experience in filming more "artsy" videos where you have more leeway to try out new, more "out the box" ideas.

The evening will start at 7pm with an introduction from Emily followed by a workshop dedicated to brainstorming a visual concept for a written Spoken Word piece.
If you would like to attend, please RSVP by Friday 17th January, and let me know whether you would like a parking space.

THURSDAY 23RD JANUARY
19:00-21:00
SPOKEN WORD WORKSHOP
BBCSCOTLAND, GLASGOW

There's no preparation needed for this workshop, so just bring your lovely selves and let's chat all things Spoken Word!

Any questions, please don't hesitate to get in touch :)

Many thanks,

Sam

Hey Ryan,

No problem at all, glad you like the zoom change. Fantastic about Michael’s TV footage, that will certainly add more context to the video.

Glad you’re happy with the two projects. I look forward to them coming out on the platform! I always like to try new things in terms of content I shoot, but my main area of interest is in people, which is why I like shooting documentary style videos. Yes, the spoken word strand would be exactly the kind of thing I’d like to get involved in. I remember the first time I seen Time For Love by Sean Lìonadh. You just knew it was going to be very popular because it was very well made and engaging throughout. So, yes I am definitely interested in that strand of filmmaking. I will keep an eye out for the junior researcher positions, because again that would be great opportunity to get involved in. I have a few ideas kicking around which I will continue to work on and I would be more than happy to help out filming on any projects, like the two just we’ve just completed, in future.

Yes, I am on the careers hub and have the alerts set up already. It’s been a good way to see what positions come up. I have previously applied for a number of positions and got an interview some time ago for the runners pool, but unfortunately never go it. It was a good experience to see how it all works though. I get the alerts everyday so I will continue to keep myself updated with that. Yes, The Nine seems like a great opportunity for aspiring filmmakers in Scotland. I take it they use freelancers and BBC employees for filming their content? See even helping out on a show like that would be something I think would be really beneficial - I’ll try and keep an eye out for any work experience via the careers hub for that. I have seen some of the clips from the Loop brand, that’s something I’d love to try and work towards.

Thank you for your helpful advice. I have started to reach out to people whose programmes I have really enjoyed towards the end of the last year. Can be difficult to always get a response but I am sure something will come of it if I continue to do it consistently. If there are any people within the BBC I am trying to reach out to - which there no doubt will be - I’ll get in touch if I can’t find any contact information.

Thank you for taking the time to pass on your advice, I really appreciate it and it’s been very useful.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

On 7 Jan 2020, at 09:20, Ryan Pasi > wrote:

Hey Jamie,

Thanks for uploading everything and making those changes, the zoom change works really well with Kiana. Everything looks good and all deliverables too.
Managed to get those clips of Michael and just need to chase up the Changing Places people this week.

No problem at all! Great to have you onboard and making content for us. These two have turned out well and really happy with your work ethic and professional style.
So in terms or other workshops and training, we have one coming up about our spoken word strand, is that kind of filmmaking something you’d be interested in?
We’re likely to be having more opportunities for contributors to work with the team as junior researchers (I think that’s the role title) for a few weeks over this year, there are a couple of people who just started. It might be something that you can apply for or perhaps after May if it’s too much of a time commitment. Aside from that, there are always stories that we need help telling so a good pair of hands is really valuable and I’ll make sure I’m passing over any ideas that you can work on and let the team know.
If there are stories you come across that you think would work well for us, then that could be a good avenue too.

Are you the BBC careershub? If not, set up a profile, you can add keywords and alerts for them for when job’s come up. We do try to let people know when things come up but this way you’ll know for sure. I think looking at opportunities in particular with The Nine is a good idea, and I’d also make sure you’re watching any videos made for BBC Scotland that come under the Loop brand. It’s similar to the kind of thing you’ve made here. There’s a shortform team here that makes things for Loop and other projects and would be something to aim for and apply for in the future.

As for the wider industry, Scotland and Glasgow especially has a brilliant market for factual programme making for all broadcasters. There are tons of indys making a range of factual that all busy. My advice is always be really systematic and list all the independent companies you can find, watch the types of shows they make, message them all asking for opportunities if they don’t list them on their site and all tell them how much you like the stuff they make. It’s a tough industry to break into in Glasgow but when you’re in and if you’re not a terrible person, you can make a real go of it and get continual work. London is easier to get started but it’s so expensive and you’ll be at the bottom rungs for much much longer.

That’s a good starting point but we should keep this convo going. I have every BBC email in my address list, if you find someone you want to meet, I can help up a meeting (within reason).

Hope that all helps!

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

Hey Ryan!

No problem at all, hope you also had a good new year! It’s no bother at all, I wanted to get the project over the line.

Michael’s Video
Glad that it works much better now. Yes there was a section where he was struggling so I asked him just to read it and I filmed him doing that. As can be seen in the clean version I have sent through. I’ve uploaded the previous version for audio soundbites, the final version with and without b-roll. Additionally, I have sent through the edited b-roll separately incase you need to move things around once you get the Scotland Tonight and The Nine footage. Hope this helps. I’ve sent across the forms and transcript, please let me know if I have forgotten anything, it has been a while since I’ve uploaded to the BBC dropbox.

Kiana’s Video
Made the changes you asked for. Unfortunately I didn’t have a cutaway of the footplates. At 0.51 I moved the smooth zoom shot so that instead it revealing an empty toilet through the door, it actually reveals Kiana sitting there talking about it. I think it works pretty well, let me know what you think! Thanks about that the last talking head shot of Kiana, I was glad with how it turned out with the colours from the books and the lighting in the background - glad you like it! I am just about to enter my final few months of my degree. Jamie

It’s all about understanding storytelling, and it’s a great opportunity to get experience in filming more “artsy” videos where you have more leeway to try out new, more “out the box” ideas.

The evening will start at 7pm with an introduction from Emily followed by a workshop dedicated to brainstorming a visual concept for a written Spoken Word piece.
If you would like to attend, please RSVP by Friday 17th January, and let me know whether you would like a parking space.

THURSDAY 23RD JANUARY
19:00-21:00
SPOKEN WORD WORKSHOP
BBCSCOTLAND, GLASGOW

There’s no preparation needed for this workshop, so just bring your lovely selves and let’s chat all things Spoken Word!

Any questions, please don’t hesitate to get in touch ☺

Many thanks,

Sam

emails.subject: Welcome to the Scottish Parliament; next week
emails.body:
Hello Angus, Jamie, Chris and Chris. Also Gayle and Juan.

Just a quick message from me to say thank you for coming on board - and at such short notice! Looking forward to getting to know each of you better in the weeks ahead.

I'm the resources and video production manager of the parliament's Broadcasting Office - I'll also be your line manager. You met me at the interview.

Bill is the office head - you'll also remember him as the chair of the interview.

And Andrew is our office administrator. He'll play a key role in ensuring you're across all team communications, pending your getting onto the parliament's IT systems etc.

It's great that we can start to get you into our system so soon; our working systems in the Broadcasting Office and associated infrastructure have been on quite a journey over the past five months and over the next few weeks, we'll be building towards getting you integrated into our team:

 * our video conferencing technology and workflow (working from home);
 * understanding the parliament as an institution - and how our work fits in;
 * getting you into the building and into the parliament's IT systems once your security clearance is through; and
 * trained up on the equipment in-house - while maintaining staffing levels which allow for safe distancing.

Gayle and Juan, who are also copied in here, joined the team very recently and are still working from home. So there are six of you who are new to this team.

Next week will be a pretty short one for you:

we'll meet you on Tuesday at 1200hrs via the Video Conference platform we use, Blue Jeans for a quick chat. We'll send you a joining link and instructions on Monday. This will just be a chat with Bill and me. Gayle and Juan are invited but might struggle to make it as they're already wrapped into business.

on Wednesday Jamie Chris and Chris will start to shadow our business on the VCs, which will be opening around 0915hs. Again, we'll provide the information for you about joining etc. I'll also set up a group meeting on Teams that morning (around 0830hrs) to talk you through things and answer any questions you might have.

You'll have worked two days by then. BUT, there's the option of joining the weekly team debrief on Thursday at 1630hrs on Teams, which will be an opportunity to meet your new colleagues as a group.

I'm also going to send you some reading and viewing material to get you across the basics:

 * the structure of this organisation and what it exists to do
 * where the staff - and particularly us in the Broadcasting Office - fit in
 * some important rules - particularly about impartiality and reputational harm

One request: starting on Tuesday, please start to "clock" your hours, including when you're doing the reading/watching work. You don't need to tot them up; just take a note of when you start and stop working (In, out, in, out etc). On a weekly basis, I'll input this information into you clocking card, until such times as you're on the system and able to do it yourself.

If you've any queries, just come back to me. You should all also have my mobile number - 07833677606; feel free to call any time.

Best wishes ...and see you next week!

Ruth

emails.subject: Re: Creative Producer (Commercial) application
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Thank you for getting back to me on this, and apologies for taking a couple of weeks to respond.

I completely understand given the length of time that has passed that your situation would have changed.

In terms of feedback on your application, I thought your showreel was really good. It showed a good variety of events you have covered, and the quality of the filming was high. I like the transitions between shots and it’s paced really well.

I did actually struggle to find your website, because the link at the bottom of your CV led to a different website (www.jamieamurray.com). This may have been because of the length of time that passed after you submitted your application, maybe your website address changed. If not, you should definitely fix that on your CV. I was able to find your website through your twitter bio, but some hiring managers may give up after the first link didn’t work.

I would also suggest putting your showreel front and centre on your website homepage. You’ve signposted it well from your homepage, but the more obvious you can make it to a potential employer the better. We had around 140 applicants for this role, and would ordinarily spend 1-2 minutes on each candidate initially to create a shortlist. Your website is really smart and your showreel is strong, so the easier it is to find the better!

Thank you for the application, and best of luck for everything you go on to produce.

Many Thanks,
Tom

--

emails.subject: Schedule for the week ahead
emails.body:
Hello Gayle, Juan, Jamie, Chris and Chris.

Please see below the weekly schedule information which has just gone up on Teams. If you've any queries, just drop me a line or call/text me: 07833677606.

Otherwise, well done - and be sure to have a good one.

Hello everyone.

Thanks again for another week of heroic work at the coal face of parliamentary business. You'll see from next week's schedule (also attached as a snip) that we've another three intense days next week but, in some ways I think (hope?!) we're starting to get a bit more structure into things.

In Holyrood: Hanif, Alan and Ben with Angus training in one cohort; and Pete, Mhairi, Clair, Ewan, Nick and Ross B in the second cohort - which itself naturally breaks into two sub-cohorts.

Working from home: Julie (Tues and Thurs), Juan, Gayle, Chris C (Wed, Thurs), Chris K and Jamie.

The aim remains to continue to get the "established" members of team familiarised/refamiliarised with equipment and workflows; also to maintain cohorts and limit cross-over into working areas to reduce the risk of contamination. While the newer members of the team are mostly focused on training on Blue Jeans (with the exception of Angus who is also learning committee audio)

But also, this week, with two late finishes, I've attempted to structure things so that early starters can get away a little earlier; and late finishers can start a little later.

Please pay attention to the new column on to the right of the schedule devoted to set-up and, for hybrid business, end-to-end tests. E2E tests are now scheduled. Also times teams are expect to be on Blue Jeans for entirely virtual sessions (and some of this is primarily for our newer colleagues who aren't familiar with working patterns). This probably needs to be finessed but it should help us plan as teams/cohorts so that people can complete their morning's work and get a proper break before picking up for business in the afternoon. So, for example, on Tuesday, Chamber E2E could be carried out by the 1200hrs (fingers crossed) finishers: Pete, Hanif and Nick.

As I mentioned yesterday, AndrewC and I are hoping to make the Individual Teams Channels for Committee meetings more of a one-stop-shop for operators, setting out:

(1) the names of attendees for you to check against arrivals and flag who's not there;
(2) the agenda (esp for captioning);
(3) the order of speakers or more general guidance on the structure of the meeting; and
(4) the Blue Jeans codes themselves.

This information shall also be emailed to Gayle, Juan, Chris C, Chris K and Jamie on the eve of their meetings.

A gentle reminder here: you all need to have this information to hand by the time you're logging into Blue Jeans for your meetings - you can't function properly without it.

Any feedback on how we're doing things and ideas for improvement will be appreciated.

Other headlines:

 * We've two first-time virtual committees meeting this week - rehearsal times and format are still to be finalised.
 * We've managed to get the TfR recording moved to Monday (Hanif and Clair)
 * And on Thursday everyone is working from home.

Finally, a reminder that it's Andrew Longbottom's last week with us - what he and Joe and Keith have had to contend with these past few months, we will probably never fully grasp. But it's incredible.

Have a lovely weekend all of you.

Ruth

emails.subject: Covid-19 - Latest Update
emails.body:
Latest from the Chief Executive, folks.

________________________________
From: McGill D (David) 
Sent: 21 August 2020 15:51
To: DL All Staff 

Dear Colleagues

You may have seen the First Minister’s statement yesterday with the latest update on the route out of lockdown. Following this, I wanted to update you on what this means for us, and for MSPs.

Continuing to work at home

Yesterday the First Minister confirmed that Scotland remains in phase 3 of the route map and that this is likely to be the case for some time to come. As such there was no date set for non-essential office workers to return to workplaces and working from home remains the default position. We also know that the Scottish Government’s route map recommends homeworking as the default at least through to phase 4. The advice was clear that continuing to work at home where possible is a significant contributor to containing the virus.

Leadership Group has therefore agreed that where possible we should continue to work from home and that this is very likely to be until at least the end of 2020. No one can predict what the situation with Covid-19 might be over the coming months, and there will be further regular updates from the Government as the situation progresses. However, to help you plan and have some degree of certainty, we wanted to set out as best we can our expectation at least for the remainder of the year. I recognise that the continuation of homeworking may be difficult and disappointing news for some colleagues. Therefore, Leadership Group, together with HR, is looking at how we can support teams and individuals during this prolonged period of working from home.

While many of you will continue to work from home, some will gradually begin to return to Holyrood because of business needs. Where this is the case, your Group or Office Head will discuss this with you. I’ve spoken before about the safety measures we have taken for those coming into the building, and I hope those working at Holyrood have found them to be reassuring, if a little different from usual. If you have any concerns however, please speak to your line manager. We are committed to continuing to support staff in the various situations that they are in.

Wellbeing Guidance

With that in mind, we will be launching some wellbeing guidance next week. This will help you to complete a personal health risk assessment and to discuss with your line manager your own circumstances and the support we can put in place as we all move forward out of lockdown. This tailored approach is one of the recommendations from our Staff Wellbeing Survey Report. HR will also provide managers with a practical guide to support team members through this process. I will send out details of this guidance next week.

MSP local offices

As I indicated above, the default positions remains to work from home, and only essential Parliament work should happen at Holyrood. However, the First Minister also announced that face-to-face advice services can resume from 24 August. This means that MSPs can now open their local offices if they consider it essential to meet constituents in person.

The Presiding Officer has today written to all Members with details about what this means for them, and I’m attaching that email for your information.

Thank you again for all you are doing and have done to date during these difficult times.

David

David McGill

Clerk/Chief Executive

Hello Kate,

Below is what I have got so far for prof develp goals. Is the correct way to go about this section of the portfolio? I am wondering what kind of evidence I need to show here, or is it a case of identifying what I want to achieve and how I will go about it, do I simply just need to explain that?

Look forward to hearing what you think.

Kind regards,
Jamie

Action plan, objectives and actions GOOD

Main Goals

Goal: THESE ARE TWO SEP GOALS

Graduate with a first class Television degree with a marketable and visually pleasing final factual project film, worthy of entry into short film competitions & FESTIVALS later in the year.

Actions:

 * Stick to my schedule of filming dates in February
 * Continue to edit as I finish filming certain sections
 * Collaborate with other to gain an outright perspective on the direction of my film.
 * Finish work in plenty of time of submission dates, to gain valuable feedback that will improve my overall grade

Goal:

Meet with a well-regarded person (producer/director/camera operator) within the factual production industry in Scotland to seek advice for tips to break into the industry and how I can market myself going forward. Please like Louise Pirie, Matt Pinder, Hannah Currie. GREAT - TICKING THAT BOX NEXT WEEK, WITH MATT, ALSO CAN U ATTEND THE BAFTA GURU EVENTS?

Actions:

 * Research and watch the recent work of Scottish based directors, decide what I enjoy most and find out what forms of content they prefer what I can access, i.e email, social media, phone call.
 * Draft email, letter and have to proof read by Kate, so I give off the correct impression.
 * Send the speculative email/letter and hopefully secure a time to meet with that person for a coffee to pick their brains and gain advice of the way forward for my career.

Goal:

Become proficient in other adobe creative cloud apps such as Photoshop CC and After Effects 2020, which will make me more employable going forward.MAYBE CHOOSE ONE LIKE AFTER EFFECTS 2020. ALSO SHOTPUT PRO NOW INSTALLED ON ONE MAC IN 6.039. CHECK WITH ME FOR ANY POTENTIAL COLLEGE ACCESS TO ANY ONLINE COURSES BEFORE PAYING....

Actions:

 * Set aside time every week to watch YouTube tutorials by Justin Odisho, who teaches people how to use such software for free.
 * Purchase an online course from Skillshare by resected industry professionals who teach these softwares.
 * Ask mentors and friends of better ability for assistance when I am unsure

Goal:

Secure freelance employment with a production company, that might hopefully lead to further opportunities post graduation. This will enable me to receive payment that will lead to me being able to afford new kit.ALSO THE JOHN MATHERS STUFF?

Actions:

Research current industry jobs and apply to the production companies, or get in touch with the production managers. ALSO THE TALENT MANAGERS AT BBC AND IWC ETC

Goal:

Keep my social media, website up to date so that potential employers can see what I have been doing to improve myself and portfolio.

Hey Jamie,

Thanks for sending this over, it looks great! Nice venue for it for sure :)
I think Katie comes across really well in it, I would say that walking to camera is pretty old school and something I’d say we can avoid when possible.

That being said, it’s a nice mix of interviews. Some of what the woman says later on about going from seeing like no one for 3 months to 200 and what that was like could be brought right up earlier.
I think focussing more on what she and the other chef say will make it come together a bit more, at the moment it feels half about their experiences in hospitality and half about this particular restaurant.
there’s a good bunch of parts that are quite specific about the space and them getting a bigger venue that I don’t think it’s super necessary to include. So focusing more on their experiences, keeping a bit about the resto owner but having less of him, I think that will get the time down a bit and give it a clearer narrative. Also near the start, there’s quite a lot of cutaways when she’s talking, is that to cover cuts? If not, I think you can have more shots of her talking, just with social media so many people watch without sound that it’s good to see her initially to get a sense of who’s talking.

From: Jamie Murray

Hi Kate,

Here is what I have so far for my bio…would be great to get your thoughts since it will be seen by industry professionals come May!

Jamie Murray is a videographer and editor originally from the Isle of Bute on the west coast of Scotland. Jamie has spent the last four years studying at City of Glasgow College where he has recently graduated with a BA Hons in television production. Jamie was an elected member of the Scottish Youth Parliament from 2015 until 2019 where he travelled to Canada, London and across Scotland campaigning on behalf of young people with key stakeholders and politicians and now focusses on shooting engaging and informative factual content for a number of organisations in Scotland.

Jamie has been involved in a number of exciting opportunities in video production, from being camera assistant working on a BBC sporting documentary with PurpleTV, working with high-profile guests at Pinewood Studios in London to now being a regular freelancer for companies such RangersTV and BBC The Social. Jamie specialises in factual content and has to date directed a number of films on issues ranging from the dangers of drink spiking, poverty, disability issues, refugees and other social issues. He is always working to ensure contributors are fairly represented and that his films reflect real issues in modern Scotland.

Jamie currently seeks traineeship roles, mentors and employment in the production industry in Scotland that will enable him to utilise his practical skills and experience and develop his knowledge in camera operation to enhance his ability to create impactful films with impactful stories worth sharing.

You can find Jamie’s work at www.jamieamurray.com and on various social media platforms with the username @JamieMurrayTV or get in touch directly via email: [email removed].

Look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Blackbaud Data Security Breach Affecting Edinburgh Napier University
emails.body:
[image: Footer] 

Dear Alumni & Friends,
Report of Data Security Incident

Edinburgh Napier University has been made aware of a data security incident affecting one of our suppliers, Blackbaud, who provide cloud computing services to store personal data.
As a result, we understand that some of your personal data may have been impacted/involved. The personal data includes your name and email address.
I am therefore writing to advise that you be vigilant to potential phishing communications and requests to provide information.
Blackbaud confirmed in its statement to Edinburgh Napier University that no credit card information or bank account details were accessed.
The Blackbaud platform which was attacked is used by Edinburgh Napier University to communicate by email with Alumni and Friends.
Edinburgh Napier University’s priority is our relationship with you as a member of our Alumni and Friends community, and the protection of your information. As soon as we were notified, we reported the breach to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) and began to seek details from Blackbaud to identify if your personal data record was included in the incident.
Blackbaud has been a respected provider of Education and Third Sector relationship management systems for more than two decades and is engaged by institutions globally. In response to the attack, Blackbaud contracted external cyber security consultants to secure the destruction of any information that was taken by the attackers. Blackbaud have confirmed to us that the information that was taken, which included your details, was destroyed as part of Blackbaud’s negotiations with the attackers. Blackbaud have also verified the quality of strengthened security systems now in place to prevent future attacks on your information.
We recognise that this is unsettling news and sincerely apologise that this happened. Blackbaud considers the mitigating actions it took should provide reassurance to those affected. As always, it is advisable that you remain vigilant for any unusual communications or requests you may receive. Information about Phishing and protecting yourself can be found here: https://www.gov.uk/report-suspicious-emails-websites-phishing. 
We will also publish updates on our website if we become aware of further important information here : https://napier.ac.uk/alumni/alumni-news/latest-news/Blackbaud-data-security-incident . If you wish to discuss this further or require more information, please contact me at [email removed]
Kind regards,

emails.subject: Re: Delay for publication
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

News vibe is mainly cause by the walking towards camera and talking, it’s such a trope for news that I think they’re trying to get away from it. The questions and responses as you mentioned were talked through previously and work well as you get that personal experience side of it. But just generally it’s quite different to self-made pieces for The Social.
The context she gives for this is that bars and restaurants are opening up and given the place is in Edinburgh and the restaurant will now be closed from after today for 16 days. It feels weird to put it out.
One option might be to record a new intro, or we can post it when the restos and bars do actually open again in the central belt.

Totally understand your frustration around this. The karate video has been difficult because of consent issues that I put to Sanjeev for forms, also for almost the whole time the classes will not have been running, in fact I’d be surprised if they started back up again. I was also concerned about people appearing in the video who have potentially fallen very ill or died and causing distress to people. You both should have been paid for the video, let me know if not. At the end of the day we couldn’t have planned for a pandemic happening and that video is just more likely for us not to be able to use it.

Sanjeev is a bit more back on it but has been in and out of hospital for the last few months and also shielding in general so haven’t been chasing him up as much.

Will keep you posted and hopefully can get this out sharpish.

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

Content Producer, BBC The Social

Facebook | Gaming | YouTube | Instagram | Twitter | bbc.co.uk

emails.subject: Final Project Film
emails.body:
Hi Jamie!

Thank for sending it over, watched it this morning. It’s a really nice piece and he’s a great find.
It’s really well shot and I thought he had a lot of interesting things to say. He gave a lovely picture of island life as well.
I think I was wondering how he got into it in the first place, it felt like there was a section from him presumably leaving Rothesay, then having his first kid and moving back that I wanted to to know more about. The current situation with the pandemic also made the edit interesting, personally, I didn’t think you needed to set it up with what was happening now, and that initial zoom video could have come at the end of it. It sort of set it up like it was going to be more about what’s happening now rather than going into pre-lockdown. That’s more of a personal choice though, and I was happy to see what was happening now regardless of where it was in the edit as it was something I immediately started thinking about.

Obviously in terms of career, things are very difficult for freelancing, but I think that TV companies are starting to plan out production. I reckon some comissions might start coming in so indies can get going again. It will understandable be very competitive and therefore even harder for new people to get their foot in the door.
I think there’s an opportunity to research all the indie’s and look at their portfolio then start reaching out to them. It’s really useful as well to get an idea of the route you want to go down, even if that changes in the future I.e if you want to get eventually get to an assistant producer role and producer director but are looking to make your start as a junior researcher. I see a lot of people who’ve directed their college/uni project and think they can just head straight into higher positions!
So definitely use this time now to research companies in Scotland that make TV, what they make and if they’re recruiting. If you’re main interest is documentary, who’s making the best docs out of Scotland? Is there a doc idea you think you could develop and make a taster for? Things like that will start to set you apart.

And obviously once we’re able to film more for The Social, it will be good to get you making as much as possible for us too.

Cheers!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

Facebook | Gaming | YouTube | Instagram | Twitter | bbc.co.uk

….for Friday Jamie, you don’t need anything like a ticket to go in though. Lori will book herself one for the same day as well, all the booking system is for is so that we don’t ever inadvertently have too many people from the dept trying to work from the same distanced spaces on the day.

Guidance in the workplace has recently changed so you now need to wear a face covering when you are moving about any communal areas of the building. You can take it off while you are sitting at your workspace but need to stick it on for going anywhere else in the building.

When you go in the main door, there is sanitiser by the door, and then a mandatory temperature checker that scans you before you go through security. Then there’s a one-way system up the stairs (it shows you in that link I sent you on before with building info), and we are on the 2nd floor – so not too many stairs! In the office, there is a one way system too, plus there are wipes and sanitiser at the kitchen hub next to our desks. The procedure is to wipe down the space you work at before you start and then again when you leave. Which desks you are to sit at are clearly marked with stickers, and have also all been figured out to allow for a suitable distance from people walking about the office too.

emails.subject: Re: Greater Glasgow & Clyde area lockdown & Updated Covid Checklist
emails.body:
Hey Jamie,

Thanks for sending this over, it looks great! Nice venue for it for sure :)
I think Katie comes across really well in it, I would say that walking to camera is pretty old school and something I’d say we can avoid when possible.

That being said, it’s a nice mix of interviews. Some of what the woman says later on about going from seeing like no one for 3 months to 200 and what that was like could be brought right up earlier.
I think focussing more on what she and the other chef say will make it come together a bit more, at the moment it feels half about their experiences in hospitality and half about this particular restaurant.
there’s a good bunch of parts that are quite specific about the space and them getting a bigger venue that I don’t think it’s super necessary to include. So focusing more on their experiences, keeping a bit about the resto owner but having less of him, I think that will get the time down a bit and give it a clearer narrative. Also near the start, there’s quite a lot of cutaways when she’s talking, is that to cover cuts? If not, I think you can have more shots of her talking, just with social media so many people watch without sound that it’s good to see her initially to get a sense of who’s talking.

Looking good so far, let me know if those notes about make sense and feels doable.
Have you got the forms for them, contrib releases and self dec stuff?

Thanks!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

Content Producer, BBC The Social
