emails.subject: Upcoming Videos for The Social | Corona Virus update
emails.body:
Hello everyone!

Hope you’re all well and coping under current world situation.
I understand for many of you, especially freelancers, this will be a challenging time. For videos that are in and have been fully complied, we’re aiming to process payments faster so there is less of a wait.

Just to update you on things with The Social.

MEETINGS
Our teams are largely working from home as it’s pretty easy for us to manage that. If you had any upcoming meetings, please do check ahead as we’re moving to phonecalls for the time being.

BE SAFE
There are a few ideas that perhaps either require interviewing someone, or going out to a location. Please bear in mind that the ongoing situation may require these shoots to be postponed. If you’re arranging to interview someone, you need to check that both you and the contributor are feeling well, if not, it’s not worth the risk of catching it and then spreading it further.
I’ve put our official risk assessment measures for this below, you’re filling out a risk assessment for a shoot, please take these precautions into your assessment.

CORONA RELATED IDEAS
As for ideas, it’s likely that we’ll get a lot of similar proposals for corona related videos.
You’re free to send these over but there will likely be more ideas that we can’t take forward for a variety of reasons. And extra compliance measures will apply.
Also given that most news stories are predominantly related to this, any other type of news and entertainment is welcomed!

We are still definitely open to ideas and if you’re stuck at home then making videos could be a good creative outlet.
Many people may start to film more where they live, I’d ask that you try to get creative where possible for your backdrops and how you use the space for filming otherwise a lot of videos may look the same I.e. Avoid white bedroom walls :)

Hope that all makes sense!

Cheers!

These are the control measures which are the official BBC advice for managing CV risk currently.

 * Wash your hands frequently with soap and water or use a sanitiser gel
 * Catch coughs and sneezes with disposable tissues or clothing, and wash your hands
 * Avoid close contact with people who are unwell
 * Avoid close contact with live or dead farm or wild animals
 * If you are feeling unwell, and/or have any upper respiratory symptoms, you should call NHS 111 (or your local medical provider)

In addition to that I think you should also think about things like

 * Don¹t eat lunch or drink on location without washing hands first
 * Wash hands or use gel after driving a pool car
 * Not shaking hands with contributors (but explaining why ­ protecting both them and us!)

On Monday, 27 July 2020, 13:47:15 BST, Private - Russell MW (Michael), MSP wrote:

Jamie

The unit exists to serve the public by making the Parliament as accessible as possible. It is also the Parliament’s duty to have a record of everything said in plenary or in committee and the unit ensures that there is a physical record of that as well as the written record that comes from the Official Report team.

A lot of the work is therefore high quality recording of what is happening. The chamber and the committee rooms are all fitted with cameras and microphones and they are on when the formal sessions are taking place. They are not on for private sessions in committee however.

The unit also provides services for the communications team which exists to publicise the parliament and disseminate information about it. The unit records interviews with members on certain topics (non political of course – things like committee conveners talking about the inquiries they are launching, or sometimes two or three MSPs reflecting on the week that has just passed.

Finally the unit makes short films that are played over the channels (each members office has a tv and there are monitors in other places too) which broadcast the committee and plenary sessions , when those sessions are not taking place. These are mostly without commentary but with music and show aspects of the campus and the work.

As the cameras are remotely operated in the committee rooms and in the chamber they do not need crew at them. The sound desk in the committee rooms and in the chamber does have someone at it though when recording is active.

I should also mention that members can get video clips of them speaking and there are often used for twitter and other social media by individual members . But they are not available for attack purposes – in other words you cant ask for someone else’s and use it against them.

I think most members take the service for granted but it is a good one.

Hope this is helpful

Good luck !

Michael

emails.subject: Karate video
emails.body:
Hello!

So plan for the video your shooting tomorrow, keen to get your thoughts on this but have some general tips on structure for it.

Structure

 * Intro from Sanjeev about why sports for disabled people are really important and also actually exist
 * we’re here at (name of place) to check out a karate class
 * Interview with instructor: why do they do it? Why’s it important? What do people get out of it? Challenges etc
 * Couple of vox pops with people taking the class, asking what it means to them and their experiences
 * Sanjeev reacts to the class or takes part
 * Sanjeev reacts at the end of the class, from either taking part partially or fully or just observing. What do you think about it? Did it look fun? Hard? Is it worth it? What were your pre-conceptions before going and what do you think now?
 * Conclusion: Sanjeev reflects on whole experience and sums up thoughts on classes that are aimed at people with disabilities

This is a good reference: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p0696nqz
B-Roll

 * Shot of centre
 * Shots of people taking the class
 * Shots of Sanjeev watching or taking part
 * Shots of any gym equipment that are relevant

VERY IMPORTANT!
Consent

 * Any one that appears as interview or is focused on in a shot needs to sign a consent form. Please also add a description of them so it’s easy to match the form to the person screen so we can check it
 * The class need to be informed about the filming and that anyone can ask to be not included or blurred. If that does come up, be really sure about being able to ID them so we make sure they don’t feature

Music

 * There might be music or loud echoey areas your shooting in, when filming interviews, if there’s music ask them to switch it off so you can get clean audio during that part, if it’s potentially a noisey area, take time to do some quick tests and check it’s all audible.

I’m travelling to Inverness tomorrow so may be hard to reach Tuesday/Wednesday so if possible give me a shout today with any queries and I’ll get back to you asap. Should be in the office till 5.

Cheers!
Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

emails.subject: IMPORTANT: INFORMATION REGARDING YOUR PAYE BOOKING WITH THE BBC
emails.body:
Dear colleague,

You may know there has been a recent to change to the PAYE payment claim process.

PAYE payments with a payment date of 4th October onwards are now automatically claimed and included in the relevant payroll, as long as:

 * You have accepted the booking in the FPP
 * A valid Right to Work is held on file for you

Now, you only need to accept your booking in the payment portal by the 3rd of the month.

Once accepted, your bookings will move to the Current Bookings tab, as usual, but you will not be able to select and action these. Instead, these will be automatically claimed overnight and will appear in your Claim History the following day. E.g. a booking accepted on the 3rd November, will be claimed overnight to be included in November payroll, and will appear in Claim History on the 4th November

Bookings accepted by 9pm on the 3rd of November will be included in November payroll.
Note: Any bookings with a claim date before 4th October 2020 will still need to be claimed as previously in the portal.
If you have any queries, please get in touch with us through our Web Form.

With best wishes,

Contingent Workforce Team,
BBC Resourcing & Talent
____________________

emails.subject: Fw: Coronavirus (COVID-19) update - summer graduations
emails.body:
FYI and remember the City of Glasgow College graduation alternative is in November,

[A close up of a logo Description automatically generated]

Coronavirus (COVID-19) update – summer graduations

Dear Students.

Please note: this message is for our Scotland-based students only.

Graduations are the highlight of the year at Edinburgh Napier and, as it stands, we hope to be able to hold our ceremonies as planned at the Usher Hall in early July.

However, the Coronavirus situation is fast moving and we are working on contingency plans to ensure that all eligible students will be able to graduate in the event that we have to postpone these particular ceremonies.

As a result, we will soon open graduation registration. This will allow us to issue graduation parchments and graduate all eligible students in absentia whether ceremonies go ahead or not.

If the ceremonies then go ahead as planned in July, all graduating students will receive a letter of congratulations from the Chancellor upon crossing the stage as you will already have your parchment.

If you cannot attend your ceremony for any reason OR if the July ceremonies are postponed, you will be offered the chance to attend an alternative date at the earliest opportunity. You will receive a letter of congratulations from the Chancellor on stage, in your gown and have the chance to celebrate your achievements with friends and family as normal.

We are continuing to monitor the situation and will send out further information once we know more.

Thank you very much for your patience at this time.

emails.body:
Hello colleagues on the Health Committee clerking team.

Here is the link for the VC for tomorrow’s meeting for you to distribute to the Convener, Deputy Convener, Members, witnesses and among yourselves.

We would ask that you distribute this later this afternoon or early evening, along with joining instructions (further below) and a request that all VC participants log in half an hour before the meeting starts in public.

Please can you email members these details and embed them in a calendar invitation for the meeting as it makes a significant difference to the workflow.

And when you get a chance, please forward us some indication as to the shape of the meeting – if an order of speakers is available, that would be great, but otherwise, it would make a big difference to get a more general indication on who might be likely to feature when.

It might also be useful for you to provide the following BIT contact information for people who are having problems joining. For this meeting, it should be:

 * Fiona Stevens (07948 276275) [email removed]

If you need any further information, just drop us a line any time.

JOINING INSTRUCTIONS

You will need Google Chome installed on your machine

 1. Open Google Chrome on your machine
 2. Copy and paste the link above for the Bluejeans meeting into Google chrome’s address bar and hit “return” to go to the page
 3. You should be joining as a Guest – enter your full name (email not necessary)
 4. Click Join as Guest
 5. Click Join
 6. Make sure your camera and audio are working by using the Test Audio button, then follow the instructions
 7. Click Join Event
 8. You should now connect to the meeting

If working with an iPad or other Apple device:

 1. Go to App store and search for BlueJeans - install
 2. Click Blue Jeans event link provided to you
 3. This will open the BlueJeans app
 4. Give permission for access to your device’s microphone and camera and enter your name if given the option
 5. You should now connect to the meeting.
If the app does NOT launch on clicking the link:

 1. Open the app
 2. Enter the meeting ID (the string of eight letters at the end of the code) – eg https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/abcdefgh
 3. Join the meeting

Kind regards
Andrew

emails.subject: Re: Karate and Katie Shannon vid
emails.body:
Hey Jamie!

All good here!

This is great! Julie’s such a star and think it’s got a nice flow and vibe to it.
I think the very very start is totally fine, a few lines in, she maybe does come across a bit nervous, I’d say the same for the last shot that her delivery does feel a wee bit nervous and also quite serious. There’s a wee bit of the walking to camera presenter vibe which is by no means the end of the world but you maybe don’t get her personality coming through.
That being said, I’d be happy to make this work, a couple of tiny edits near the start and we’d also get a big stat on screen as I think it gets a bit lost with her just saying it.

I totally understand if Katie wants to re-shoot, it’s also totally nerve racking putting yourself out there in a video and want her to be happy with it.
Do you think if you were to refilm that start part that it would be a while before you can do it?

Good stuff about the karate video, I’d expected it to be noisey so do the best you can! Any issues or stumbling blocks, give me a shout.

Cheers!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

emails.body:
Hi Jamie

Good to hear from you. The week is filling up a bit now, but I could potentially meet for coffee tomorrow lunch if that’s not too short notice? Or maybe Friday depending on how things pan out. 

Let me know how you’re fixed where you are and we’ll figure something out. 

Cheers

Matt

Sent from my iPhone

> On 24 Feb 2020, at 16:48, Jamie Murray wrote:
> 
> ﻿
> Dear Matt,
> 
> My name is Jamie Murray, a fourth year television student studying in Glasgow. Thank you for passing your email on to my lecturer Kate Cotter. I really appreciate it.
> 
> I was very taken aback by your documentary on the Margaret Fleming murder trial. I am originally from the Isle of Bute and therefore I am used to driving past the house where Margaret had lived. I remember very clearly people talking about the case when the news first broke and I felt your documentary done an incredible job at highlighting the failures in the system whereby a vulnerable person can simply be forgotten about. It is a very tragic story but one that is definitely worth being told. Having cameras in the court room was a really great insight into that world also and something I have never really seen before. Very informative!
> 
> I’d love to meet with you to get your advice on career progression, the pathway that you have taken and just general tips for moving forward once I complete my education. I have been very lucky to receive a short-term freelance opportunity whilst I finish my degree and that begins next week. So, would you be available at some point this week to meet with me?
> 
> I understand you will be very busy, Kate had mentioned about being in an edit for another project, so I don’t want to get in your way at all or keep you long. It would just be very beneficial to meet you.
> 
> Look forward to hearing from you.
> 
> Kindest of regards,
> Jamie
> Jamie Murray
> Videographer
> www.jamieamurray.com
> 
> 
>

Thanks,

emails.subject: Re: Thanks for coming!
emails.body:
Hi Jamie!

I’m so glad you enjoyed it, thanks again for coming along.

Grief has been touched on, but not extensively so if you have any ideas around that then please let me know! And yes, we can totally look at matching you up with a spoken word artist, don’t worry we’re not expecting you to write your own stuff if you don’t want to haha! Now that I know you’re on the books to film spoken word I’ll keep you in mind for the next time we need a filmmaker (which should hopefully be soon).

Thanks again and all the best,

Emily

Emily Brown
Researcher | BBC The Social

From: Jamie Murray >
Date: Saturday, 25 January 2020 at 17:37
To: Emily Brown - Digital >

Hey Emily,

Thank you very much for your email and for the workshop on Thursday. It was very helpful and enjoyable.

I have replied with some feedback to Paul - all positive. Hopefully there will be similar workshops in the future that I could attend!

Thanks for sending your number through. I am going to have a think about some spoken word pieces and see if I can come up with something that might work well on screen. I have an idea for one on the topic of grief - I know, fun topic! But, I feel it could be a worthwhile project. I just wondered, has this topic already been comprehensively covered via spoken word on BBC The Social?

Thank you for sending through the Homeless Joe materials, they are a great reference. I do remember watching the film when it was first put out. It is a fantastic example of how, like you mentioned, spoken word filmmaking can bridge the gap between factual and drama. You feel emerged in the story, yet understand it as example of real life and the struggles people can face.

Recently, I have been helping other contributors realise their factual pieces and I have really been enjoying that so far. I would love to work with some spoken work artists who are looking to get their films made also - should the opportunity come up. So if there is any scope for pairing a videographer up with an artist, I would definitely be interested.

Thanks again for the workshop and I look forward to speaking with you in the future.

Enjoy the remainder of your weekend.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie
Jamie Murray
Videographer
www.jamieamurray.com

You have my email now, and also here is my number, so feel free to get in touch anytime with spoken word related questions or queries: 07380417727

I’ve attached my shotlists for Homeless Joe, the one in chronological order (called shot list) and the one in order of the shoot (called shoot shot list). I hope you find these helpful, and again, any questions just shout! Here’s the finished film for reference: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p06jp49t

Whenever you’re interested in doing your next spoken word film, just let your producer know and I’ll be able to collaborate with them to help find you an artist to work with! And of course, if you already have an artist in mind then even better!

To: Paul McFadyen

Hello Paul,

1) Yes! I found the workshop to be very useful and inspiring. It was a great chance to ask the people who have created such films all about the technical and storytelling elements that go into spoken work films.

2) I enjoyed the exercise where we were given a poem and asked to visualise it how we saw fit. It was interesting to see how others interpreted the poem and crucially, I benefited from watching the finished film as it showed me where I could improve on my storytelling.

3) I will take the advice and guidance forward with my in future projects for sure! Yesterday was also a great chance to meet other creatives working with the social.

I'd love to get involved in as many workshops as possible in future as I am always looking to improve and try new things.

emails.subject: TV Job Question!
emails.body:
Jamie

The unit exists to serve the public by making the Parliament as accessible as possible. It is also the Parliament’s duty to have a record of everything said in plenary or in committee and the unit ensures that there is a physical record of that as well as the written record that comes from the Official Report team.

A lot of the work is therefore high quality recording of what is happening. The chamber and the committee rooms are all fitted with cameras and microphones and they are on when the formal sessions are taking place. They are not on for private sessions in committee however.

The unit also provides services for the communications team which exists to publicise the parliament and disseminate information about it. The unit records interviews with members on certain topics (non political of course – things like committee conveners talking about the inquiries they are launching, or sometimes two or three MSPs reflecting on the week that has just passed.

Finally the unit makes short films that are played over the channels (each members office has a tv and there are monitors in other places too) which broadcast the committee and plenary sessions , when those sessions are not taking place. These are mostly without commentary but with music and show aspects of the campus and the work.

As the cameras are remotely operated in the committee rooms and in the chamber they do not need crew at them. The sound desk in the committee rooms and in the chamber does have someone at it though when recording is active.

I should also mention that members can get video clips of them speaking and there are often used for twitter and other social media by individual members . But they are not available for attack purposes – in other words you cant ask for someone else’s and use it against them.

I think most members take the service for granted but it is a good one.

Hope this is helpful

Good luck !

Michael

Hi Jamie

I work next to (when we’re in the office!) Paul McFadyen from The Social, and he recommended you to me when I was asking him if he could think of anyone who might be able to help us out with a bit of edit support we need at the moment.

We are in the middle of making a chat show strand which is part of TUNE (our music series for the BBC Scotland channel / iPlayer) and we could really do with an extra pair of hands helping out as a researcher two days a week for a short while to help us with the social deliverables we need to create to accompany each prog.

Paul wasn’t sure if you had time at the moment, so I thought I would enquire? Here is more info about what we are looking for.

We work with Adobe Premiere, and can supply a macbook with this software, so would be looking for someone who is adept at using Premiere, and able to cut down / square / subtitle video that we provide from the series. We are working remotely at the moment, although a day in the office would probably be required to collect the laptop and get the necessary software installed as well as returning it.

We’d be looking for an initial day to sort out laptop tasks on 12 or 13 Oct, thereafter we’d be looking for help on Mondays and Tuesdays, starting Mon 19/Tues 20 Oct and going on until Mon 23/ Tues 24 Nov. It would be 13 days in total.

Let me know what you think or if there’s anything else you’d like to know. If you are interested / free, I can introduce you to our Production Manager Eileen who would be able to discuss rate and set up a contract.

emails.subject: Bio
emails.body:
Hi,

Love the showreel. Think the volume build too slowly at the start so we start adjusting thinking we have it down too low..very slight edit here..OK with you?

Jamie Murray is a videographer and editor originally from the Isle of Bute. He has spent the last four years studying at City of Glasgow College where he has recently graduated with a BA Hons in Television Production. Jamie was an elected member of the Scottish Youth Parliament from 2015 until 2019 and he travelled to Canada, London and across Scotland campaigning on behalf of young people with key stakeholders and politicians. He is focused on shooting engaging and informative content for a number of organisations in Scotland.

Jamie has gained some great and varied experience so far as a camera assistant working on a BBC sporting documentary with PurpleTV, working with high-profile guests at Pinewood Studios in London to now being a regular freelancer for companies such RangersTV and BBC The Social. Jamie specialises in factual content and has to date directed a number of films on issues ranging from the dangers of drink spiking, poverty, disability issues, refugees and other social issues. He is always working to ensure contributors are fairly represented and that his films reflect real issues in modern Scotland.

Jamie is interested in traineeship roles, mentors and employment in the production industry in Scotland that will enable him to utilise his practical skills and develop further knowledge in camera operation to enhance his ability to create impactful films around stories worth sharing.

Kate Cotter

emails.subject: Re: Videography - Calums Cabin
emails.body:
Hello Jamie
Thank you so much for coming back to us, Keriin passed on your email.
At present we are looking at a couple of options, we have a few small home made by families videos and would like them put together and cut into one, maybe about 3 mins long depending on the content and the other thing that we are after is a walkaround of the cabin and cottage and potentially some of the Glasgow flats when there are no families in, so when someone is looking to book a holiday then they can see first hand where they are coming, these will naturally be shorter in length.
For this type of coverage, the first film that I was talking about would be shown at events and to potential charity partners etc, the second would be embedded into our website and put on social media platforms.
If you would be able to give us rough time scales in this regard that would be great, ie how long it would take to create, edit etc and what the potential costings would be.
Thank you.
Caroline
From: Keriin McMillan 
Sent: 10 January 2020 15:22
To: Marion MacLean ; Siobhán O'Hara ; enquiries 

Hello,

Here’s the reply I got from Jamie, if anyone has any ideas or any further questions that I could ask etc.

Let me all know what you think.

Thanks
Keriin

From: Jamie Murray >
Sent: 09 January 2020 16:50
To: Keriin McMillan >

Hello Keriin,

Thank you for your email.

Not too busy at the minute as I am just getting started back at uni so this is probably the best time to get in contact.

I would love to help out with some filming and editing work for Calum’s Cabin.

In terms of the specification for the video, I think there is a few ways we could go with it. I have made many promotional videos for charities and organisations, which feature interviews and some which simply use text to give context to the video. Both styles can work well, depending on the length of videos you would like me to create. With this project, would it be two separate videos just for use as promotion of the two properties? Or is it one video, featuring both properties?

Also, it is worth considering where this video will be used. Is it for distribution only on the website, or would it be used on social media platforms? Because the length of the video for some social platforms are limited.

I found this video on the website: https://youtu.be/4QXSPxtcQlo. Is this the kind of thing you mean in terms of content? I think we could upgrade this video if that is the kind of thing you are after.

So, moving forward if we can decide on exactly what kind of video we are going for, how many videos and what needs to be included in the video then we can start to discuss the logistics, timings for shooting the videos and pricing for filming and editing.

I look forward to hearing from you and thank you for coming to me with this opportunity.

Have a lovely weekend.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

Jamie Murray
Videographer
www.jamieamurray.com

emails.subject: Goodbye for now!
emails.body:
Hello!
I just want to say thank you all for the continued work and keeping up the creativity, whether we’ve been working together for a few years or it’s more recent, I’m really proud to see what’s been achieved under very challenging circumstances.

As some of you may know I’m taking an extended leave starting in the next couple of weeks for paternity leave!
I’m very pleased to say that Emily Brown will be taking over while I’m away!
She started as a contributor and has been working as a researcher on the team since Feb 2019 and is going to be a brilliant producer for your work over the next few months. Many of you will have met her before but it’s worth dropping her a line to say hello in the new year after the 6th.

Couple of things to think about for this handover

 * Emily and I are going through all your current ideas that are in production so she’s across it but in some cases a quick reminder and sending her the script will be very handy for reference.
 * There’s about 80 of you! So will just ask you to have patience in the first few weeks while she gets up to speed

Your future with The Social!
If you’ve just joined fairly recently, view 2021 as your chance to try and get as much time and experience under your belt working with us, it’s a brilliant opportunity and you’ll get out of it what you put into it.

If you’ve been with us for a few years, it’s time to start thinking about your next steps and career. Are there bigger ideas you could develop and we can help put you in touch with the development team? Is there more of a strand or series you could work on that might work for TV further down the line? Do you want to work more behind the scenes like our team do or in other parts of the industry? All these points are good to think about no matter what stage you’re at so take some time to think over.

Cheers!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social

[thesociallogo]

Facebook | Instagram | Twitter | bbc.co.uk

emails.subject: Re: Introductions
emails.body:
Hi Jamie

Unfortunately since I first contacted you the BBC has withdrawn the hot desking facilities it had offered staff on a rota basis as restrictions in Scotland have become tighter, so we are having to manage with only skeleton access to PQ when absolutely necessary. As security wouldn’t let you in without being hosted by one of us to begin with, it would also mean someone else having to come in to enable that, so we have worked it this way to avoid any need for you to come in.

That would be great if you were able to start editing on your own software though and might be an interim solution. What version of Adobe are you using? (just so we can check we can transfer between machines ok – sometimes this can be a problem if we have older versions). This problem with the licence install happens every single time we start a new person in our team and is incredibly frustrating. The process to get the software remotely has changed since it was installed on my machine, but I think it might either come up as a notification, or you might be able to force it quicker via the ‘self service’ option which you find in the BBC blocks on the top right on the screen. Someone in IT has to click ‘approve’ before this process starts though, and that probably hasn’t happened yet.

This is a link to the more or less final version of ep 1 (this is pre-dub – the files you will get have been through the dub)

Lori will need to advise which bits will be going into which social cuts though as it will be reliant on music rights which can be rather complicated on social, so it’s not quite as straightforward as lifting a section and subtitling it in every case.

To give you an idea of what our social deliverables look like though – this is a link to the deliverables folder for a recent Howling to the Wind iplayer special we published. https://www.dropbox.com/sh/yjaf6lq0wflq0nb/AADOR6MlJA_2LD8dePCSkbqba?dl=0

We also have quite a lot on iplayer at the moment, which you can find here: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0002x06/episodes/player

And the BBC Scotland YT channel doesn’t get the most views, but it’s the easiest way to link to a collection of some of our social cuts, you can find it here https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL5tFdO7wRDHnVd0OI1qXZbaudhmIfqagA

Taking a look through all this tomorrow morning would be a good use of your time. As Lori will be returning from a week of leave she will have a lot of emails to get through first so might be a little later on in the day before she gets in touch properly.

Cheers

Susie

From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: 23 July 2020 15:39
To: Kate Cotter 

Hello Kate,

I hope you are keeping well and beginning to enjoy your summer as restrictions lift.

I wanted to get in touch to let you know I have been fortunate enough to get a job interview (online) next Tuesday for a job at the Scottish Parliament, for the role as a technical operator.

I wondered if you either know of anyone working there/or who has worked there. And also if you have any advice for me?

I have attached the job description to this email.

The panel will consist of in case you've heard of any of those people:

Bill Ward, Head of Broadcasting, Chair of the Panel
Ruth O'Reilly, Resources & Video Production Manager
Alison Urquhart, Human Resources Officer.

Look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Jamie

Jamie Murray
Media Content Creator

Dear Jamie Archibald

Edinburgh Napier University is pleased to confirm that we have processed your Graduation application.

This message is to confirm that you have registered to Graduate in absentia, but may attend a future ceremony.
Parchments will be posted to your home address as soon as is reasonably practical after the date of the graduations. Parchments posted to UK addresses will be sent recorded delivery and will require a signature. Please ensure that you maintain your home address in your eStudent Record.

If you have not already been awarded by the University, your application is provisional at this stage, and is dependent on the ratification of your results at the programme board of examiners in June 2020. Results will be released on your eStudent Record on Thursday 9 July 2020.

If you have any further queries regarding your Graduation application, please reply to this email. A member of staff from Student Administration Services will be in contact shortly after receipt of any email enquiry.

Regards

emails.body:
Hey,

So we’d need to approve it before anything gets filmed, each person involved will need to sign a self declaration form on the day.

You’ll need to fill out the Covid Checklist and also a risk assessment that sets out how you plan to film and information about location. If you can work out a way to film socially distant, and can confirm processes for cleaning down before and after the shoot, it will give it a fighting chance to get approved. You might need to set out that you’ll record questions and nodding reaction stuff seperately, which to be honest is pretty common for factual tv.

If you can get that over to me early next week, I’ll send it on from our side and get back to you asap.

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Thank you for getting back to me. We have sourced someone who can do the work.

Not to worry as it was a very specific request.

Thank you again,

Jonny

Sent from my iPhone

On 13 Aug 2020, at 20:12, Jamie Murray wrote:

﻿

EXTERNAL EMAIL: Check it is safe before you click.

Hello Jonny,

I am good thanks, yourself? Thanks very much for your email, it's much appreciated.

In the interest of being completely upfront with you, I must admit I have never actually worked on a project that has required stream back for an interview shoot 'as-live'.

Having said that, I have had some discussions with my flatmate who is also a videographer and has completed 'live-streaming' type projects before, and I think I can offer some help although it may not be exactly what you need.

In terms of the two options, I don't think the first one would be feasible for me as I wouldn't have access to Blackmagic unit that would be required. There would be a possibility of using a second computer and connecting that to second camera which could also be used via zoom, however I am not sure if this would suit your needs?

With the second option, I do believe there is a method where I could connect my Sony A7III to my computer using a capture card and use it almost like a webcam via zoom...This is obviously a much simpler option, but if you need both options to be available then I am not sure I will be able to help, given the short timeframe and not having access to the required equipment. I have lav/radio mics so the audio would be fine as well as soft boxs for the lighting set-up.

I look forward to hearing your thoughts. If you still think any of what I have proposed may be of help, please let me know and then I could propose a price for this.

Apologies if this isn't of any help to you, but I will completely understand if it isn't.

Have a lovely weekend.

Kind regards,
Jamie

From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: 13 February 2020 14:14
To: [email removed]

Hello,

My name is Jamie Murray and I am applying for the exciting role of Film Director for the Scottish Social Services Awards 2020, following my rewarding experience of taking part last year. I'm currently a fourth-year BA Hons student at City of Glasgow College studying Television Production.

Since taking part in the SSSA in 2019 (for which, I directed two films: #SSSA19 Category 5: Shelter Scotland and #SSSA19 Category 4: Dundee City Council and Partners) I have filmed a number of other projects of a similar nature. During the summer, I was commissioned to create a one minute video for the Scottish Parliament focussed on a Syrian refugee called Mounzer: https://youtu.be/ru_LITxyt5M.

Additionally, I have filmed and edited various short form videos for the Rangers Charity Foundation: Everyone Anyone: VI Football,
Glen Kamara launches new Foundation partnership and Rangers Charity Foundation Dream Day.

Furthermore, I also create videos for BBC The Social that can all be found here: BBC | Jamie Murray. Since I directed two videos last year for the SSSA, I have undertaken many projects of a similar nature and tackled various difficult topics such as death, disabilities and injustice. I believe these experiences make me a great candidate who can be trusted to take sensitive subject matter and create interesting impactful films, worthy of being shown at the SSSA in 2020.

On Monday, 16 March 2020, 16:15:12 GMT, Ryan Pasi > wrote:

Hello everyone!

Hope you’re all well and coping under current world situation.
I understand for many of you, especially freelancers, this will be a challenging time. For videos that are in and have been fully complied, we’re aiming to process payments faster so there is less of a wait.

Just to update you on things with The Social.

MEETINGS
Our teams are largely working from home as it’s pretty easy for us to manage that. If you had any upcoming meetings, please do check ahead as we’re moving to phonecalls for the time being.

BE SAFE
There are a few ideas that perhaps either require interviewing someone, or going out to a location. Please bear in mind that the ongoing situation may require these shoots to be postponed. If you’re arranging to interview someone, you need to check that both you and the contributor are feeling well, if not, it’s not worth the risk of catching it and then spreading it further.
I’ve put our official risk assessment measures for this below, you’re filling out a risk assessment for a shoot, please take these precautions into your assessment.

CORONA RELATED IDEAS
As for ideas, it’s likely that we’ll get a lot of similar proposals for corona related videos.
You’re free to send these over but there will likely be more ideas that we can’t take forward for a variety of reasons. And extra compliance measures will apply.
Also given that most news stories are predominantly related to this, any other type of news and entertainment is welcomed!

We are still definitely open to ideas and if you’re stuck at home then making videos could be a good creative outlet.
Many people may start to film more where they live, I’d ask that you try to get creative where possible for your backdrops and how you use the space for filming otherwise a lot of videos may look the same I.e. Avoid white bedroom walls :)

Hope that all makes sense!

Cheers!

These are the control measures which are the official BBC advice for managing CV risk currently.

 * Wash your hands frequently with soap and water or use a sanitiser gel
 * Catch coughs and sneezes with disposable tissues or clothing, and wash your hands
 * Avoid close contact with people who are unwell
 * Avoid close contact with live or dead farm or wild animals
 * If you are feeling unwell, and/or have any upper respiratory symptoms, you should call NHS 111 (or your local medical provider)

In addition to that I think you should also think about things like

 * Don¹t eat lunch or drink on location without washing hands first
 * Wash hands or use gel after driving a pool car
 * Not shaking hands with contributors (but explaining why ­ protecting both them and us!)

emails.subject: Hospitality idea
emails.body:
Hello!

Got your forms, have started the process with our team to get approval so will update you about that asap. I’m on holiday till the 2nd so will make sure you have a contact in case things need picked up while I’m away. I think the plans for filming look good, you should be able to all film inside as long as you’re keeping 2 m distance, but that will need signed off from our saftey side.

Script
Can you draft up your intro and outro, it will be good to have an idea of what you’re going to say to wrap this vid, it’s important that you’re bringing your own personality and experience to it, otherwise it falls very much into more presenter type news style which doesn’t fit with The Social as much. There should be no question as to why you’re part of it if that makes sense.

Story
Stuart is a bit on the older side so the key here is capturing how this time has affected younger staff who typically work in hospitatlity. It’s really important that a good chunk of time is talking to a younger person on the team and capturing how they feel, it’s more effective than Stuart just saying how he’s tried to help. Good to have his contribution but don’t want to make it too much about him. Any questions, give me a shout and will get back to you tomorrow before I’m off.

Will be in touch asap and if I don’t have answer end of play tomorrow, will message with team contacts so you can pick it up with them while I’m off.

Cheers!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

emails.subject: Ep 2 Sharon Rooney social cuts
emails.body:
Hi Jamie

Welcome back, here we are at ep 2! Lori will send you over the material you need and the drive for this, and will be in touch later with what is needed for the YouTube cut, but here is what it would be great if you could look after first of all.

1x1 cut (1080x1080)
You’ll need to recreate the graphics again this week as per Lori’s guide last week.
Shots might need repositioned same as last week in order to fit the square

Shot order:

Start with discoball Kerr which you can lift from 01.33 - 01.35 in the yungblud square cut and open Sharon’s social cut with that

Then from Sharon’s video:

Add the whole section 02.43 – 03.23 “pick one tune that makes you feel homesick….I’m back!”
Caption Kerr Okan and Sharon Rooney at the start of this as last week using phosphate font, not putting over faces and holding for about 2seconds or what feels natural

04.32 – 04.35 – add in this interstitial of Kerr with the record player

09.25 – 10.04 “pick a tune that reminds you of your happiest memories on set… this is it, like – I’ve done it”

09.19 – 09.21 - add in the interstitial of Kerr with the clapper board

14.38 – 14.55 “one last question for you…. (Kerr laughing)”

Add subtitles and gradient
Add the 1080x1080 DOG
End with Kerr and the discoball sequence and iplayer logo (lift from yungblud ep)

-----

Once this is done and subbed, send it over to me and I will look at it and proof the subs. Once that’s done, you’ll then be able to do the IGTV same way you made it last week.

While the file is with me to look at the subs could you please do the thumbnails for the square and IGTV? emails.subject: Message from Faculty Dean
emails.body: Hello my dear students, My name is Elodie, and for those i have never met, I am the dean and director of the faculty of Creative Industries. I just wanted to drop you a short line before summer kicks in. First of all, congratulations to each and everyone of you for making it to the end of this particularly weird academic year. I know it has been hard and so difficult on so many levels for you, both in College and sometimes at home. So you deserve all my admiration for keeping up, cracking on and making it to the finish line. After I saw your work for the online show, my first reaction was pure amazement and surely enough did I feel humbled by your talent and your commitment to succeed, whatever it took. You are in my eyes, both artists and warriors! You must certainly be one of the most deserving graduate promotion of all times. On Wed, 25 Nov 2020, 10:29 Jamie Murray, 
wrote:

> Hello Jane,
>
> Just wanted to send you an email to say I am planning on starting the edit
> on the second piece 'Battles o'er & bloody field of Flanders.' Are you
> still happy for me to go ahead with the edit? You had mentioned the 30th of
> November as a date for the video? I have detailed below a few things that
> may improve the second video, but it would require filming again:
>
> First of all, the re-recording of the pieces again would require every
> band member to record their performance with the exact same settings.
>
> To do that requires everyone to adjust something in their phone settings
> called the 'video framerate'. On an android: you launch open Camera and
> jump into Settings > Video Frame Rate and select "30". For an iPhone, open
> Settings > Camera > Record Video and select > "1080p HD at 30fps". By doing
> this it will ensure all video files are of the same quality and settings,
> which should prevent some people's performances from seeming out of sync as
> they did last time.
>
> The second thing that would improve the final video would be when Neil
> records his track that everyone else uses as a base track when recording,
> it would really help if he could count down from 4 and clap his hands
> together before he then picks up his instrument and begins playing. When
> everyone else records their piece, they will need to listen to Neil
> counting and ALSO clap when he does. This would then enable me to
> completely sync everything up and if everyone records at the same settings
> then I would be able to use everyone's camera.
>
> One final note, it would be nice if we could see everyone's face during
> their recordings and not just people's arms. I always feel it makes it more
> personal, but obviously, that is down to personal preference.
>
> This, inevitably, would require everyone to re-record their pieces and
> Neil would need to create a new backing track for others to follow where he
> counts down and claps his hands so I appreciate this may take some time and
> may push us past the date of the 30th, what are your thoughts?
>
> If you would like me to go ahead with the versions I already have, I am
> happy to give it a go, but having watched those clips I envision a few
> syncing problems with will vastly reduce the quality of the video.
>
> I do think, therefore, if you are still happy to, we could have a go at
> filming it again with those instructions I outlined above and I think that
> would, in the end, make for a much more polished video for Rothesay
> Pipeband. Also, if you are happy with just the video that made before and
> you wish to go ahead with the second one, that is absolutely fine.
>
> Look forward to hearing from you.
>
> Kindest of regards,
> Jamie

From: Jamie Murray

To: Kate Cotter 

Hi Kate,

Here is what I have so far for my bio…would be great to get your thoughts since it will be seen by industry professionals come May!

Jamie Murray is a videographer and editor originally from the Isle of Bute on the west coast of Scotland. Jamie has spent the last four years studying at City of Glasgow College where he has recently graduated with a BA Hons in television production. Jamie was an elected member of the Scottish Youth Parliament from 2015 until 2019 where he travelled to Canada, London and across Scotland campaigning on behalf of young people with key stakeholders and politicians and now focusses on shooting engaging and informative factual content for a number of organisations in Scotland.

Jamie has been involved in a number of exciting opportunities in video production, from being camera assistant working on a BBC sporting documentary with PurpleTV, working with high-profile guests at Pinewood Studios in London to now being a regular freelancer for companies such RangersTV and BBC The Social. Jamie specialises in factual content and has to date directed a number of films on issues ranging from the dangers of drink spiking, poverty, disability issues, refugees and other social issues. He is always working to ensure contributors are fairly represented and that his films reflect real issues in modern Scotland.

Jamie currently seeks traineeship roles, mentors and employment in the production industry in Scotland that will enable him to utilise his practical skills and experience and develop his knowledge in camera operation to enhance his ability to create impactful films with impactful stories worth sharing.

You can find Jamie’s work at www.jamieamurray.com and on various social media platforms with the username @JamieMurrayTV or get in touch directly via email: [email removed].

Look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Re: Disability and Employment video on TV
emails.body:
Hey Michael,

Let’s keep working on getting you able to film solo for the time being. That’s a good anniversary to mark but we’d not be able to get anything for that time but it’s a good shout for reposting. A big challenge right now is that we’re not able to film indoors with anyone in their house, and with the impending news about the Tier system in Scotland, we’re not sure what the filming restrictions might be but I suspect it will be even harder to film content. Also since it’s raining all the time, filming outdoors is a bad option.

I sent an email with suggestions for your own video making so let’s continue with that in the mean time.

Cheers!

emails.subject: Hardship Fund - HF4475-4431-1146-8658 0403 (OFFICIAL)
emails.body:
OFFICIAL

Dear Jamie Murray

Thank you for your application for financial support through the Newly Self Employed Hardship Fund.

We have been unable to process your application as you have not included the following supporting documentation:

 1. Evidence of active trading (bank statements covering 3 months January 2020- March 2020). Please submit bank statements for 3 months January to March 2020. Please ensure bank statements show your name, your address, sort code, and account number, and monthly list of all transactions. Require January 2020 Full Statement.

 * MANDATORY: Bank statements (business or personal) covering 3 months from January to March 2020 showing income and outgoings from self-employment.
 * Please ensure documents submitted are e.g. pdf files - we cannot accept screen shots of banking transactions.

 1. UTR or 1st supporting document of active trading
Please submit another copy of UTR evidence showing your name, if this is not possible please select one from list below

And ,

 1. 2nd supporting document of active trading
Please submit one of the following from list below (must be different piece of evidence to that submitted for 1st supporting document evidence).

 * A supplier or reseller trade account (active). E.g., documentation or a statement showing a trading account with a wholesaler, an eBay seller account, Amazon Business, Etsy, etc.
 * Valid business insurance in the trading name of the business or name of the applicant
 * VAT Registration Number. This should be a letter or electronic communication. Officers are not required to verify with HMRC.
 * Marketing materials for your business, e.g. business website, active social media. Web links, social media account name (LinkedIn, Facebook, other). Officers should check for authenticity, and that the website or social media includes content covering the period during which the applicant claims to have been trading, i.e. that the content was not created just to support the application.
 * Other evidence of business activity to support your claim. This could include correspondence with a supplier or customer, a testimonials, a photo of a vehicle bearing the applicant's details (so long as these match the details on the form).

emails.subject: Re: Karate and Katie Shannon vid
emails.body:
Hey Jamie,

Yeah let’s go ahead, I’m happy with that and would rather push ahead. I think she comes across a bit nervous but with more practice that will get ironed out :)

Karate

This is nice! I think the edit and pace of it works well. Sanjeev is nice and has good delivery. Such a big improvement from his first vid to this.
I understand your concern about the instructor being a bit older but I think cause Sanjeev is carrying it and leading it, the video works and is good to highlight.
I do think it will likely pull in an older audience but there’s not a huge amount we can do about that. What would have been better is if the presenter was taking part and getting more of his experiences, that helps avoid it feeling more like a news piece, however obviously that wasn’t possible and think it’s worked out well.

I think you’ve managed the sound well, couple of edit notes below and pops and clicks and one shot change if possible.

 * 00:51 Audio pop
 * 02:23 the audio sort of crashes in here, can you put a little fade up to soften it. Would it be possible to cut back to Sanjeev talking here?
 * 02:46 audio click
Main big question is about consent for the people taking part in the class, did you get forms or on screen consent from them?

Cheers!

Ryan Pasi (he/him)
Content Producer, BBC The Social
0141 422 6974
[thesociallogo]

From: Jamie Murray >
Date: Wednesday, 26 February 2020 at 11:22
To: Ryan Pasi >

Hey Ryan.

No worries then. Once I have heard back from Katie I can let you know when I can deliver the video. I am away next next weekend and my birthday is the weekend after, but I have proposed shooting on Sat 14th March, the day of my birthday but I can only do the morning that day as I have other things planned - so need to wait to hear Katie's availability.

Karate video is looking good so far...only thing is with the interview with the people taking part in the class who have disabilities, their interviews are not really useable at all and Sanjeev had to continue to ask many questions as they struggled to answer the questions. So with that, we have the main interview with the man who leads the class and a carer/helper who assists and takes part in the class, both of which are good, I am just worried as they class leader is middle ages and carer is an older male as well. Hopefully with Sanjeev's opening and closings we can fit in with the BBC The Social demographics.

I had to say no to Kiana this time unfortunately as she has asked about filming on the 14th, which I had initially said no to because it's my birthday, but as i've just explained I have offered that morning to Katie to get her video over the line asap.

Just about to reply to Emily! Looks like a great idea for a spoken work piece, something I am very interested in. And the one about a young carer is definitely something that sounds like it could be very powerful as well - so I'd love to explore that. So it is looking like the weekends in the later march/early April where I would have my next availability. I know that sounds far away, but it is because of taking on this full time opportunity, and being busy with other things planned next weekend and the weekend after! If that is too long, if you are looking to get those videos out sooner than that - I totally would understand.

And thank you for your reassurance, I really appreciate the opportunity to film these videos for The Social. As this current freelance opportunity ends in May, I will 100% be looking to use all my time after that (because I will have finished uni by then also) to work on other videos and as many projects as possible as well.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

Videographer

On Monday, 24 February 2020, 14:57:54 GMT, Ryan Pasi > wrote:

Hey Jamie!

All good here!

This is great! Julie’s such a star and think it’s got a nice flow and vibe to it.
I think the very very start is totally fine, a few lines in, she maybe does come across a bit nervous, I’d say the same for the last shot that her delivery does feel a wee bit nervous and also quite serious. There’s a wee bit of the walking to camera presenter vibe which is by no means the end of the world but you maybe don’t get her personality coming through.
That being said, I’d be happy to make this work, a couple of tiny edits near the start and we’d also get a big stat on screen as I think it gets a bit lost with her just saying it.

I totally understand if Katie wants to re-shoot, it’s also totally nerve racking putting yourself out there in a video and want her to be happy with it.
Do you think if you were to refilm that start part that it would be a while before you can do it?

Good stuff about the karate video, I’d expected it to be noisey so do the best you can! Any issues or stumbling blocks, give me a shout.

emails.subject: Welcome to WhoisMatt's Newsletter! Here's where to start...
emails.body:
a:hover{color:#1b8ede;border-bottom-color:#1b8ede}
.button:hover{color:#fff;background:#666}

Hey friend,

My name is Matt Johnson and I'm the creator of whoismatt.com. I
wanted to thank you so much for signing up for my email
newsletter!

Whether you are new to wedding videography, or you have been
creating wedding films for years, I know that the things that I
am going to share with you are going to help take your wedding
filmmaking to the next level, no matter what your current skill
level.

What you can expect from me:

For the next two weeks, you'll receive one email per day with
tips and tutorials for how to improve your filmmaking, editing,
and business. You can also expect some gifts and bonuses too. :)

After those two weeks, I will generally email you once per week
with a new tutorial or guide that will keep improving your films.

I'll also let you know about new courses and premium educational
resources I create, but only if I think they will truly help you.

Sound good? AWESOME!

Here's what you need to know to get started...

STEP 1:

Whitelist and prioritize all emails from "Matt WhoisMatt
Johnson".

This is super important! You'll be getting my best tutorials and
tips to take your filmmaking to the next level, but if my emails
aren't getting through you are going to miss out.

So please take the following easy actions to make sure that you
don't miss these emails:

1) Follow the whitelisting instructions for your email provider
at this page: Whitelisting Instructions (
)​

2) If you use Gmail, be sure to "drag" any emails from your
"Promotions" tab to your "Primary" inbox so you actually see
them.

3) Create a "WhoisMatt" folder where you can archive these emails
AFTER you read them so you can find them again in the future.

STEP 2:

Take a few seconds and join the "Learn Wedding Filmmaking with
Whoismatt" Facebook Group and "Like" the WhoisMatt Facebook Page
as I post a ton of news and updates there:

​Join the Learn Wedding Filmmaking with WhoisMatt Facebook Group

)​

Thanks again for becoming a subscriber!

Warmly,

Matt Johnson

P.S. You are going to love the next few days, I have a ton of
exciting gifts coming to your inbox that are going to take your
filmmaking to the next level!

Tomorrow you'll be receiving the first gift. :)

emails.subject: Re: Contact details
emails.body:
Hi Jamie

Sorry for the delay in getting back to you, I was waiting on the drummers
feedback!

Just a couple of things which have come up!

After the first part of the tune the hands and fingers aren't moving in
time to the tunes - this could be the recording as you suggested! Is it
possible to start off with everyone on the main screen then cut to old war
images /photos of the band at armistice (I can provide)? I know this means
you actually only see us playing for a very short period but I think this
is preferable to hands moving out of sync!!

Is there any way of muting the drummers other than Alex and Megan? Perhaps
amplify Megan and this will help with the beats being correct?

Could you turn up the background music played by the fiddle and accordion
(both chords and melody)?

As a intro screen perhaps something that says - Rothesay and District Pipe
Band
Battle of the Somme
Lest we forget

I hope this makes sense. I'll quickly gather some images of the band and
old war photos that may be useful.

Thanks

Jane

emails.subject: Scottish Parliament security questionnaire
emails.body:
Dear Jamie

We have received a request from HR that you be given security clearance in order for you to be issued with a Parliament Security Pass, therefore, please find attached a security questionnaire for you to complete.

There are two ways to complete this:

 1. Print off a hard copy and complete in black ink.

Or

 1. Complete the fields on your computer then print it off.

You must then sign the declaration, in black ink, on pages 7 and 9 and send the form to:

The Scottish Parliament

Security Office

Q1.05

Holyrood

Edinburgh

EH99 1SP

COVID 19 WORKING

In addition to the above instructions, we would ask that you also email your scanned forms to [email removed], this will ensure that your clearance is dealt with should we need to work out-with the Parliament building

ID CONFIRMATION FORM

You are also required to return the attached ID confirmation form, which should be signed and authorised by either your present employer/line manager or someone of good-standing in the community (e.g. doctor, teacher, civil servant etc.) that has known you for 5 years or more, along with a copy of your passport or driving licence. We cannot accept forms completed by family members

It is very important that you complete the form in full and return it to us as quickly as possible as you will not be issued with a pass until the clearance process is complete.

Should you require any further assistance, do not hesitate to contact me on the number below.

Kind regards
Carol Cameron

Security Office
Q1.05
Holyrood
Edinburgh
EH99 1SP

Tel: 0131 34 86558

emails.subject: Offer of Employment - Scottish Parliament
emails.body:
Dear Jamie

My colleague Claire Kearney will be your point of contact with regard to your pre-employment process.

Further to our conversation of yesterday, I have attached our letter confirming that you have been recommended for appointment as a Technical Operator on a fixed term basis. We briefly discussed that there would be flexibility around the days you will work, however, I would recommend that you speak to Ruth O'Reilly directly to discuss further options, or indeed should you need to discuss anything in relation to the role. Ruth can be contacted on 07833 677606.

The letter outlines next steps in terms of our pre-employment process, and to allow us progress quickly, we would ask that you complete and return the relevant documents/information as soon as possible.

Our Security Team will get in touch to take forward your clearance.

Finally, could you please return the completed Pension Questionnaire and Bank Details form directly to Claire.

In the meantime, if you have any further questions then please don't hesitate to contact either me or Claire.

Kind regards.

Alison

You are invited to our “Filming Spoken Word” workshop on Thursday the 23rd of January at BBC Scotland Pacific Quay, in Glasgow, hosted by Emily Brown, from The Social who is also a filmmaker with lots of experience in filming Spoken Word.

Spoken Word on The Social has become incredibly popular and is in constant demand. We have lots of Spoken Word artists, however we’re lacking in Spoken Word filmmakers! The aim of the workshop is to bring filmmakers from The Social together, to network and learn some tips about filming Spoken Word.

Many filmmakers don’t feel confident in filming Spoken Word as they may not have a poetry background, however there is no need! It’s all about understanding storytelling, and it’s a great opportunity to get experience in filming more “artsy” videos where you have more leeway to try out new, more “out the box” ideas.

The evening will start at 7pm with an introduction from Emily followed by a workshop dedicated to brainstorming a visual concept for a written Spoken Word piece.
If you would like to attend, please RSVP by Friday 17th January, and let me know whether you would like a parking space.

THURSDAY 23RD JANUARY
19:00-21:00
SPOKEN WORD WORKSHOP
BBCSCOTLAND, GLASGOW

There’s no preparation needed for this workshop, so just bring your lovely selves and let’s chat all things Spoken Word!

Any questions, please don’t hesitate to get in touch ☺

Many thanks,

Sam

emails.subject: College closes for face to face teaching and moves to online delivery
emails.body: Hi all, The college building closes at 5pm today. The kit room is in operation with Murray and Iris there until 4:00pm. There are 4 laptops available if anyone needs one let us know and anyone who had booked kit or wants any can come collect it before 4:00pm. I will continue to work and support you on your modules through to the end. This will be done remotely but contact and support will continue via email/phone and MyCity. The college counselling service, student services and funding etc will all continue online/remotely. We really appreciate that this is a challenging time for everyone and hope you will keep in good communication with us. We will update you on any progress or changes here too. Dissertation will continue on schedule and Lorna and myself are available to help with your draft work. Professional Development will continue on schedule and I am available to help with your draft work. Final Project paperwork will be as before but I appreciate many of you won't be able to complete your shoots, try and get as much together as you can in the next while. We are working with Napier to find a solution as to how to assess the module fully in light of these challenges. I will keep you updated. We are mainly focussed on your overall wellbeing and will ensure that it is possible to get through your modules remotely as best as possible. You are encouraged to stick to Government guidelines about social distancing and where necessary self isolating. It is an unprecedented time and Edinburgh Napier University and City of Glasgow College are keen to get all students through as smoothly as possible. Email me if you have any immediate questions. More updates soon. Best wishes, Kate Cotter Lecturer & Programme Leader BA Television School of Creative Industries 0141 375 8317 & 07986 268 602 City of Glasgow College 190 Cathedral Street Glasgow G4 0RF

Hey Jamie,

Thanks for sending this over,

I think it’s a well put together pitch. It’s good to see the stats on how much it affects young people especially.
It’s something that you could probably pitch to our development team or at least get some feedback on it.
What I would recommend first is to record a short taster or pilot episode, using yourself perhaps as the first subject? Just something that would help to give an idea of the potential style and vibe of it. Using yourself first would help since you’re not asking another person to go into an emotional state for something that might not go forward or that they’d have to do it again. Obviously that does put that pressure on you though.

Let me know what you think as an initial step! Also just watch your spelling, there’s a good few errors in the pitch.

emails.subject: Some more induction material
emails.body:
Hello Jamie, Chris, Chris and Angus,

I've some more induction material here for you to "enjoy" over the next few days.

In the important links document (attached) there are some items you currently can't access (and I know: it's a curse). But among the ones you can, I'd ask you to pay particular attention to the codes/policies I've highlighted under the Staff Handbook, which can be summed up thus:

 * The good reputation of this organisation is of critical importance
 * While the parliament is a benevolent and supportive employer, behaviour which could impact on the parliament's reputation or draw unfavourable press attention is a very, very bad career move here.
 * The impartiality of the Parliamentary Service staff (of which you are now one) is of critical importance. Behaviour which displays political bias or which even gives and insight into how you might vote is also a poor career move here. The clerks - who are at the interface between the members and the rest of the organisation - talk about having a "clerky face": it means interested but neutral. But that is how embedded this principle of impartiality (and a certain composure) is here.
 * Be VERY careful how you engage on social media from now on. No rows. No politics.
 * If you've a potential conflict - political, business or otherwise, you do need to let Bill or myself know about it.

I've also attached here:

 1. The organisation's strategic plan
 2. The organisation's delivery plan (I've not read it in a while, but I suspect events have rather overtaken it)
 3. Values and behaviours framework

We can talk about these things another time but the key takeaway is that top line of the Strategic Plan - ie what we, as a body of staff, are here to support the members in in doing: representing the people of Scotland by passing legislation, scrutinising the government and debating topics of national importance. Everything else flows from that.

I also mentioned to you the values and behaviours framework. Do have a look at this and start to digest it. There is a fair amount of corporate-speak there but there is a genuine culture shift taking place in this organisation and these values underpin it. The idea is that it's no longer just about us delivering (although we DO have to do that). It's about how we do it; how we treat people and what we build along the way. Time will tell how far this approach goes but I've seen significant change inside this organisation in the past year - and it's refreshing.

Also, I spoke to you about clocking your hours. I'm attaching here a snip of my clock card so you understand what I'll need you to jot down (until you've got the system running yourself): basically "in", "out", "in", "out" etc. No need to tot the hours etc.

And finally, finally ....

Here (below) is a snip of the schedule, which you'll eventually get fuller access to. You'll get a fresh version of this on Friday and you'll see your names sprinkled liberally around....

That OK?

Thanks again - and great to see you all here and on board.

Ruth

emails.subject: IGTV cut guide
emails.body:
Hello! I’ve written up a wee guide to cutting for IGTV, hope this makes sense:

-The max frame ratio when the video appears in someone's feed is 4x5, so subs/branding should be kept within that frame size for the first 15 seconds, at which point Insta will force you to go to IGTV to watch the rest of the video, which will be in a full vertical frame (9x16)

 -I’d copy my square cut into a new sequence that’s 9x16 (1080x1920), then highlight the first 15 seconds and make it into a nested sequence. Go into the nested sequence and at the top go to your sequence settings and change the aspect ratio to 4x5 (1080x1350).

-Scale up the images in the nested sequence to fit the frame size

-Go back to your vertical sequence, duplicatd the nested sequence and scale up + add gaussian blur to the one underneath so there’s no black bars top and bottom.

-Make sure all your subs are on the same video layer and nest them too, so you can move them all at once. The first 15 seconds of subs should be within the 4x5 frame, and then they should move down after 15 seconds, I just move them with position keyframes.

-Do the same as above with the BBC Scotland DOG (don’t need to nest this though)

-Scale up the rest of your vertical sequence to fit the 9x16 frame – often an interview shot will need repositioned so it’s centred.

-Export as H.264

I’ve attached a couple of screen grabs of my project from a recent IGTV cut which might help the written instructions make more sense! Please shout me if you have any questions.

Rachel

To: "[email removed]" 
Cc: Susan Miller , Lori Duncan 

Hello! I’ve written up a wee guide to cutting for IGTV, hope this makes sense:

-The max frame ratio when the video appears in someone's feed is 4x5, so subs/branding should be kept within that frame size for the first 15 seconds, at which point Insta will force you to go to IGTV to watch the rest of the video, which will be in a full vertical frame (9x16)

 -I’d copy my square cut into a new sequence that’s 9x16 (1080x1920), then highlight the first 15 seconds and make it into a nested sequence. Go into the nested sequence and at the top go to your sequence settings and change the aspect ratio to 4x5 (1080x1350).

-Scale up the images in the nested sequence to fit the frame size

-Go back to your vertical sequence, duplicatd the nested sequence and scale up + add gaussian blur to the one underneath so there’s no black bars top and bottom.

-Make sure all your subs are on the same video layer and nest them too, so you can move them all at once. The first 15 seconds of subs should be within the 4x5 frame, and then they should move down after 15 seconds, I just move them with position keyframes.

-Do the same as above with the BBC Scotland DOG (don’t need to nest this though)

-Scale up the rest of your vertical sequence to fit the 9x16 frame – often an interview shot will need repositioned so it’s centred.

-Export as H.264

I’ve attached a couple of screen grabs of my project from a recent IGTV cut which might help the written instructions make more sense! Please shout me if you have any questions.

Rachel

That being said, it’s a nice mix of interviews. Some of what the woman says later on about going from seeing like no one for 3 months to 200 and what that was like could be brought right up earlier.
I think focussing more on what she and the other chef say will make it come together a bit more, at the moment it feels half about their experiences in hospitality and half about this particular restaurant.
there’s a good bunch of parts that are quite specific about the space and them getting a bigger venue that I don’t think it’s super necessary to include. On Monday, 16 March 2020, 16:15:12 GMT, Ryan Pasi > wrote:

Hello everyone!

Hope you’re all well and coping under current world situation.
I understand for many of you, especially freelancers, this will be a challenging time. For videos that are in and have been fully complied, we’re aiming to process payments faster so there is less of a wait.

Just to update you on things with The Social.

MEETINGS
Our teams are largely working from home as it’s pretty easy for us to manage that. If you had any upcoming meetings, please do check ahead as we’re moving to phonecalls for the time being.

BE SAFE
There are a few ideas that perhaps either require interviewing someone, or going out to a location. Please bear in mind that the ongoing situation may require these shoots to be postponed. If you’re arranging to interview someone, you need to check that both you and the contributor are feeling well, if not, it’s not worth the risk of catching it and then spreading it further.
I’ve put our official risk assessment measures for this below, you’re filling out a risk assessment for a shoot, please take these precautions into your assessment.

CORONA RELATED IDEAS
As for ideas, it’s likely that we’ll get a lot of similar proposals for corona related videos.
You’re free to send these over but there will likely be more ideas that we can’t take forward for a variety of reasons. And extra compliance measures will apply.
Also given that most news stories are predominantly related to this, any other type of news and entertainment is welcomed!

We are still definitely open to ideas and if you’re stuck at home then making videos could be a good creative outlet.
Many people may start to film more where they live, I’d ask that you try to get creative where possible for your backdrops and how you use the space for filming otherwise a lot of videos may look the same I.e. Avoid white bedroom walls :)

Hope that all makes sense!

Cheers!

These are the control measures which are the official BBC advice for managing CV risk currently.

 * Wash your hands frequently with soap and water or use a sanitiser gel
 * Catch coughs and sneezes with disposable tissues or clothing, and wash your hands
 * Avoid close contact with people who are unwell
 * Avoid close contact with live or dead farm or wild animals
 * If you are feeling unwell, and/or have any upper respiratory symptoms, you should call NHS 111 (or your local medical provider)

In addition to that I think you should also think about things like

 * Don¹t eat lunch or drink on location without washing hands first
 * Wash hands or use gel after driving a pool car
 * Not shaking hands with contributors (but explaining why ­ protecting both them and us!)

Here is the link for the VC for tomorrow’s meeting for you to distribute to the Convener, Deputy Convener, Members, witnesses and among yourselves.

We would ask that you distribute this later this afternoon or early evening, along with joining instructions (further below) and a request that all VC participants log in half an hour before the meeting starts in public.

Please can you email members these details and embed them in a calendar invitation for the meeting as it makes a significant difference to the workflow.

And when you get a chance, please forward us some indication as to the shape of the meeting – if an order of speakers is available, that would be great, but otherwise, it would make a big difference to get a more general indication on who might be likely to feature when.

It might also be useful for you to provide the following BIT contact information for people who are having problems joining. For this meeting, it should be:

 * Marie McHugh (07702 318910) [email removed]

If you need any further information, just drop us a line any time.

JOINING INSTRUCTIONS

You will need Google Chome installed on your machine

 1. Open Google Chrome on your machine
 2. Copy and paste the link above for the Bluejeans meeting into Google chrome’s address bar and hit “return” to go to the page
 3. You should be joining as a Guest – enter your full name (email not necessary)
 4. Click Join as Guest
 5. Click Join
 6. Make sure your camera and audio are working by using the Test Audio button, then follow the instructions
 7. Click Join Event
 8. You should now connect to the meeting

If working with an iPad or other Apple device:

 1. Go to App store and search for BlueJeans - install
 2. Click Blue Jeans event link provided to you
 3. This will open the BlueJeans app
 4. Give permission for access to your device’s microphone and camera and enter your name if given the option
 5. You should now connect to the meeting.
If the app does NOT launch on clicking the link:

 1. Open the app
 2. Enter the meeting ID (the string of eight letters at the end of the code) – eg https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/abcdefgh
 3. Join the meeting

Kind regards
Andrew

Please note that I am currently working from home and can be reached via email & Microsoft teams.
