Hey Jamie!

All good here!

This is great! Julie’s such a star and think it’s got a nice flow and vibe to it.
I think the very very start is totally fine, a few lines in, she maybe does come across a bit nervous, I’d say the same for the last shot that her delivery does feel a wee bit nervous and also quite serious. There’s a wee bit of the walking to camera presenter vibe which is by no means the end of the world but you maybe don’t get her personality coming through.
That being said, I’d be happy to make this work, a couple of tiny edits near the start and we’d also get a big stat on screen as I think it gets a bit lost with her just saying it.

I totally understand if Katie wants to re-shoot, it’s also totally nerve racking putting yourself out there in a video and want her to be happy with it.
Do you think if you were to refilm that start part that it would be a while before you can do it?

emails.subject: Re: Edit researcher request for BBC Scotland digital?
emails.body:
Hi Jamie

Great to hear from you and thanks for getting back to me so quickly.

This all sounds great and we would prefer to work around your existing commitments rather than ask you to make any changes with a longer term contract on our behalf.

I think we would be able to make Friday/Mondays work – it all hinges on our dub day which should be a Wednesday. As long as we can get final dubbed versions back in time to get them to you for a Friday (we would taxi them to you on a drive – am I right in saying you are Glasgow based?), we could do that – if that works for you? The series is likely to publish on a Thurs, which makes working on the edits midweek too close to the wire, and it would be easier if you were working on it on days the producer of this show is available to consult with rather than a weekend. Each week will have its own specific set of music rights issues to be dealt with, so it would save time if you are both able to talk about it as you go.

So – could we pencil this with you please? Lori (the producer who runs TUNE) is chasing those dub bookings so we just want to make sure that we can get the slot we have asked for on a Wed to make this plan work. I’m surprised we haven’t heard back from them yet so we should hear this week about those bookings.

Also please be introduced to Eileen our Production Manager. She will be able to discuss rates with you and also get the contract set up when we get that 100% confirmation from you and dubbing that we can get it all to work out.

It’s always great to meet and bring new people into our team so we are looking forward to working with you,

Speak to you soon,
Thanks,

Susie

emails.subject: Re: 2 Videos
emails.body:
Hey Jamie,

Thanks for uploading everything and making those changes, the zoom change works really well with Kiana. Everything looks good and all deliverables too.
Managed to get those clips of Michael and just need to chase up the Changing Places people this week.

No problem at all! Great to have you onboard and making content for us. These two have turned out well and really happy with your work ethic and professional style.
So in terms or other workshops and training, we have one coming up about our spoken word strand, is that kind of filmmaking something you’d be interested in?
We’re likely to be having more opportunities for contributors to work with the team as junior researchers (I think that’s the role title) for a few weeks over this year, there are a couple of people who just started. It might be something that you can apply for or perhaps after May if it’s too much of a time commitment. Aside from that, there are always stories that we need help telling so a good pair of hands is really valuable and I’ll make sure I’m passing over any ideas that you can work on and let the team know.
If there are stories you come across that you think would work well for us, then that could be a good avenue too.

Are you the BBC careershub? If not, set up a profile, you can add keywords and alerts for them for when job’s come up. We do try to let people know when things come up but this way you’ll know for sure. I think looking at opportunities in particular with The Nine is a good idea, and I’d also make sure you’re watching any videos made for BBC Scotland that come under the Loop brand. It’s similar to the kind of thing you’ve made here. There’s a shortform team here that makes things for Loop and other projects and would be something to aim for and apply for in the future.

As for the wider industry, Scotland and Glasgow especially has a brilliant market for factual programme making for all broadcasters. There are tons of indys making a range of factual that all busy. My advice is always be really systematic and list all the independent companies you can find, watch the types of shows they make, message them all asking for opportunities if they don’t list them on their site and all tell them how much you like the stuff they make. It’s a tough industry to break into in Glasgow but when you’re in and if you’re not a terrible person, you can make a real go of it and get continual work. London is easier to get started but it’s so expensive and you’ll be at the bottom rungs for much much longer.

That’s a good starting point but we should keep this convo going. I have every BBC email in my address list, if you find someone you want to meet, I can help up a meeting (within reason).

Hope that all helps!

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

Thanks for sending this over,

I think it’s a well put together pitch. It’s good to see the stats on how much it affects young people especially.

Hi Jamie,

How are you?

My name is Jonny MacCann, I am the Video Production Manager for an Irish sports broadcaster called Off The Ball, we have a shoot upcoming on the 21st of August for which we need a videographer who can stream back a feed for an interview.

We are looking for a couple of options for an event we are looking to run.

There are two options, if you could give me a price for both please:

emails.subject: Corporate Bulletin - Wednesday 19 August 2020
emails.body:
Hello Gayle, Juan, Chris, Chris and Jamie.

Please see below the corporate bulletin ... a new feature of your lives ...

Speak soon.

Ruth

From: Chief Executive Office
Sent: 19 August 2020 15:25
To: DL All Users 

[CBHEaderPNG (002)]

Dear All

Welcome to this week's Corporate Bulletin.

If you would like us to include something in a future edition of the bulletin, please send us an email.

Thanks

Corporate Bulletin Team

Public Service Pensions - consultation on changes to the transitional arrangements to the 2015 scheme

If you were an active member of any of the civil service pension schemes (classic, classic plus, premium or nuvos) on or before 31 March 2012 and continued to be a Civil Service Pension member on 1 April 2015 (or left and then returned within 5 years) this will be of interest to you.

Civil Service Pensions has asked us to bring to your attention the UK Government's decision to commence a Public Consultation exercise about proposed changes to all the main public service pension schemes, including the Civil Service Pension scheme, in order to remove the discrimination found in the changes made in 2015 following the introduction of the alpha scheme. Further information about the McCloud Judgement, the Public Consultation exercise and how to respond can be found on the Civil Service Pensions website.

Mailroom and Post Office - Further change to opening hours

Earlier this week we emailed to say that the Mailroom and Post Office would open on Thursdays. Please note that a change has been made and both services will now open on Tuesdays and Wednesdays only for the next few weeks. We will keep this under review and update you on any further changes.

The Mailroom will operate from 9am to 2.00pm. There will be a single mail delivery and collection service late morning. Any ad hoc or urgent collections can be accommodated until 2.00pm. You can email Mailroom colleagues at [email removed] or telephone on x85140.

The Post Office will open 10.30am to 2.30pm. In line with the Scottish Government guidance in relation to all Post Offices, please wear a face covering in the Post Office unless you are exempt. Please note that bulk stamps for Members can continue to be ordered from [email removed].

Blue, Desk Cleaning Tokens - SPS Offices

[cid:[email removed]]

Blue, square, cleaning tokens have been placed in SPS offices to allow staff working at Holyrood to indicate to our cleaning colleagues that their desk has been used. The supply of tokens can be found near the anti-bacterial spray and blue paper-towel roll which have been placed in offices for you to use if you wish. Simply put a token on your desk before you leave and it will be cleaned overnight. If the token is still there in the morning, the desk has been missed so please call the Facilities Management Helpdesk on 0131 348 5100 to let them know.

As always, keeping a clear desk allows for cleaning to be done thoroughly. Please also keep tea points clear of all cutlery and crockery.

There is a more regular cleaning regime in the MSP block and we are therefore not operating the token system there.

Group Discussion Sessions: Returning to Holyrood / Local Offices

Everyone working at and for the Scottish Parliament is continuing to adapt to significant change. As business resumes more fully again, more of us will be returning to Holyrood, while many of us will continue to work from home. To help you prepare for a return to Parliament, the HR Office has arranged for facilitated group sessions for people who are currently working at Holyrood and for those returning to Holyrood in the future. This will provide an opportunity for people to share each other's experiences, discuss any anxieties, as well as any practical concerns. Separate sessions are available for booking for MSP staff returning to work either in their constituency offices or at Holyrood.

Sessions will be held on

 * Tuesday 25 August, 10.00am - 11.00am
 * Tuesday 25 August, 1.00pm - 2.00pm (MSP Staff Only)
 * Wednesday 2 September, 10.00am - 11.00am (MSP Staff Only)
 * Wednesday 2 September, 1.00pm - 2.00pm
 * Monday 7 September 10.00am - 11.00am
 * Monday 7 September, 1.00pm - 2.00pm

SPS and MSP staff can sign up via SPLearning (search for Group Discussion) or by emailing HR, and Members can sign up by emailing HR. A 'Microsoft Teams meeting invite to take part will be sent the day before the event.

Procurement Training Resources

A reminder that a number of helpful resources are available on SPLearning. These are suitable for all levels of involvement in purchasing, whether you are a purchaser using EASEbuy or corporate card, or are involved in a quotation or tender process, or just want a simple overview of the Parliament's procurement processes.

You can access these resources, via the Procurement tab, under 'My SPCB Essentials' on SPLearning.

Childcare Vouchers - Reminder

Have your childcare arrangements changed? Or are you now in receipt of the increased provision to nursery hours?

If so, please let us know as this could have an effect on your entitlement to childcare vouchers. Changes may include receiving government funding for pre-school education, children commencing primary school or if you have registered for the Government Childcare Tax Free Scheme.

Further information on the Childcare Voucher Scheme can be found here.

Please contact Dawn Gibbons, Pay and Pensions Team Leader or Derek Stein, Pay and Pensions Manager if you have any queries.

Recording Your Hours on TRS - SPS Staff

We currently have temporary arrangements in place which ensure that if you have been unable to complete your full working hours a credit is automatically added to your flexi balance on TRS to ensure you suffer no detriment. In order for this to operate effectively it is important that you record the actual hours you work and that you are keeping TRS up to date.

If you do not wish to have your flexi balance automatically updated, for example, if you want to reduce your accrued flexi balance by working less hours, you can do this by:

 * informing HR Systems of the week(s) you do not want the automatic update to be applied, or
 * requesting flexi leave on TRS in the usual way. Any hours you clock on the day you have flexi leave booked will automatically count towards your balance. For example, if your standard hours are 7 per day but you only intend to work 5 hours, if you have booked a days flexi leave the system will credit you with the 5 hours worked and will not top you up with the 2 hours you chose not to work.

We are currently working with our software supplier to develop a solution which will enable you to opt out of the automatic no detriment update and we hope to have this in place later this month. A further update will be provided on that nearer the time.

Further details can be found in the Remote Working: Guidance for Staff document on the Staff Handbook.

Information on Our Response to Covid-19 Coronavirus

FAQs for Members, Members' staff and Parliament staff can be accessed on our online hubs: for MSPs/MSP staff and SPS staff.

Pass Studio

The Pass Studio has re-opened for Members, Members' staff and SPS staff on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. In order to observe social distancing rules and ensure the Pass Studio can be cleaned after each visit, we have introduced a booking system. Members, Members' staff and SPS staff can arrange appointments using this link. Appointments will be 10 minutes long and can be booked from 10:00am until 3:00pm. If an appointment outwith these times is required, this can be arranged by emailing [email removed].

Contacting the IT Helpdesk

The IT Helpdesk can be contacted directly by phone on (0131 34) 86100 or by email at [email removed]. Please call if your request is urgent. If using email, please include a contact telephone number and the times you will be available - this avoids a further exchange of emails and helps colleagues to deal with your enquiry quickly.

FM Helpdesk Opening Hours

FM Helpdesk has extended its opening hours on business days from 9am to 6pm with a break at 1:00pm - 1:30pm. Non business days will be 9:00am to 5:00pm.

Mailroom and Post Office Services

Both services will now open on Tuesdays and Wednesdays only for the next few weeks.

The Mailroom will operate from 9am to 2.00pm. There will be a single mail delivery and collection service late morning. Any ad hoc or urgent collections can be accommodated until 2.00pm. You can email Mailroom colleagues at [email removed] or telephone on x85140.

The Post Office will open 10.30am to 2.30pm. In line with the Scottish Government guidance in relation to all Post Offices, please wear a face covering in the Post Office unless you are exempt. Please note that bulk stamps for Members can continue to be ordered from [email removed].

"Click and Collect" Lunch Service

A new "Click and Collect" lunch service, operating from the Members' Room, is available to everyone.

The service offers the same menu as the Garden Level Restaurant but gives you the option of ordering in advance. You are encouraged to use the new "Click and Collect" service to help reduce queuing in the Garden Level Restaurant.

You can pre-order your lunch from 3:00pm the day before until 11:00am on the day via this link.

Central Taxis

Please follow the link for some information on measures that Central Taxis is taking in response to Covid-19.
Useful Contacts
Colleagues are contactable but only by email. Here are some useful contact emails:

 * HR email: [email removed]
 * General Enquiries: [email removed]
 * FM helpdesk: [email removed]
 * IT helpdesk: [email removed] - If emailing, please provide a contact number and times you will be available.
 * Allowances Office: [email removed]

Update Your Details

Everyone has been asked to update their details on the SP Alert system so the Parliament can contact you by text message or home email out of hours if necessary. Contact details are drawn from e-HR. To ensure that you receive messages sent through alert, please check the Alternative Contact Details on your e-HR record and update if required. On e-HR, select 'Personal Information' and 'Employee Details'. Have a look at the top tips for accessing eHR for guidance. The next scheduled upload is 21 August. To ensure your details are included, please check and update your e-HR record by the end of Thursday 20 August.

If you are not on our payroll system, for instance if you are a contractor or agency staff, you will not be on our SP Alert system. Please make sure that arrangements are in place within your office or line management so that you will be informed promptly about any urgent messages.

We've no redeployment opportunities this week.

emails.subject: Bio
emails.body:
Sarah Tainsh is a recent graduate of Edinburgh Napier University’s film undergraduate program, where she specialised in sound recording and sound postproduction. Her passion for sound stemmed partially from her love of music and twelve years as a viola player, partially from her mild addiction to YouTube videos about foley artists, but mostly from her love of sonic storytelling. In her final year she undertook the role of sound designer and mixer on four short films - an even mix of fiction and documentary - and did location recording for three. She is currently seeking traineeship roles in sound recording while pursuing the possibility of further study in sound design for film. Also interested in factual filmmaking, she has directed several short documentaries during her time at university, varying from an abstract depiction of an epileptic seizure to a poetic insight into body image through the words of a life model. She also directed a documentary in Shanghai in partnership with Shanghai Normal University students, and is keen to pursue more international film collaborations in the future.

emails.subject: Greater Glasgow & Clyde area lockdown & Updated Covid Checklist
emails.body:
Hello everyone,

You will have likely seen the news around Glasgow area lockdowns, this means until it lifts, any filming in those areas with people outside your household needs to be put on hold. There are exceptions around care givers and single households who are in a relationship with another, i.e couples, but as ever it’s an evolving situation, so please keep in touch if you had any plans to film and are now unsure about whether they can go ahead.

It’s also quite possible more areas could go into lockdown so again, the best thing is to keep in touch and we can advise.

I’ve also attached an updated Covid Checklist form that needs to be completed to any filming. Please use this going forward.

On that, thanks to everyone who’s been adapting to the new processes around risk assessments and covid paperwork. I know it can be a pain but it’s important to complete and ensure everyone is staying safe.

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

Content Producer, BBC The Social

On Tuesday, 20 October 2020, 14:03:30 BST, Rachel Coburn > wrote:

Hello! I’ve written up a wee guide to cutting for IGTV, hope this makes sense:

-The max frame ratio when the video appears in someone's feed is 4x5, so subs/branding should be kept within that frame size for the first 15 seconds, at which point Insta will force you to go to IGTV to watch the rest of the video, which will be in a full vertical frame (9x16)

 -I’d copy my square cut into a new sequence that’s 9x16 (1080x1920), then highlight the first 15 seconds and make it into a nested sequence. Go into the nested sequence and at the top go to your sequence settings and change the aspect ratio to 4x5 (1080x1350).

-Scale up the images in the nested sequence to fit the frame size

-Go back to your vertical sequence, duplicatd the nested sequence and scale up + add gaussian blur to the one underneath so there’s no black bars top and bottom.

-Make sure all your subs are on the same video layer and nest them too, so you can move them all at once. The first 15 seconds of subs should be within the 4x5 frame, and then they should move down after 15 seconds, I just move them with position keyframes.

-Do the same as above with the BBC Scotland DOG (don’t need to nest this though)

-Scale up the rest of your vertical sequence to fit the 9x16 frame – often an interview shot will need repositioned so it’s centred.

-Export as H.264

I’ve attached a couple of screen grabs of my project from a recent IGTV cut which might help the written instructions make more sense! Please shout me if you have any questions.

Rachel

emails.subject: Automatic reply: URGENT: Former MSYP request regarding ScotParl TV
emails.body:
Thank you for taking the time to contact me. This is an automatic reply to let you know your email has been received.

There is a strict Parliamentary protocol that Members of Parliament can only take up matters on behalf of their own constituents. I’d be obliged, therefore, if you could include your home address and postcode in your email to me. If this was not included originally, please send your original email again and include this information.

Please note that at the moment I am receiving a large volume of mails and calls from constituents concerned about the impact of coronavirus (COVID-19) and I will be prioritising these and other urgent cases.

For the latest health guidance on coronavirus please visit www.nhsinform/scot

For up to date information from the Scottish Government please visit https://www.gov.scot/coronavirus-covid-19/

Travel information and workplace advice is available at www.hps.scot.nhs.uk

If you do not have symptoms and are looking for general information please call the NHS Inform free helpline on 0800 028 2816

It is also important to take care of your mental health at this time. Visit www.breathingspace.scot

Any businesses with questions relating to the impact of COVID-19 are urged to call the business helpline number, 0300 303 0660. This will be open Monday to Friday 8.30am to 5.30pm. Callers should select option one to speak to the COVID-19 team.

I will also be posting local updates and any community news on my website www.michaelrussellmsp.scot and on my Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/michaelrussellsnp

Best wishes

Michael Russell MSP

Argyll and Bute

On Monday, 16 March 2020, 16:15:12 GMT, Ryan Pasi > wrote:

Hello everyone!

Hope you’re all well and coping under current world situation.
I understand for many of you, especially freelancers, this will be a challenging time. For videos that are in and have been fully complied, we’re aiming to process payments faster so there is less of a wait.

Just to update you on things with The Social.

MEETINGS
Our teams are largely working from home as it’s pretty easy for us to manage that. If you had any upcoming meetings, please do check ahead as we’re moving to phonecalls for the time being.

BE SAFE
There are a few ideas that perhaps either require interviewing someone, or going out to a location. Please bear in mind that the ongoing situation may require these shoots to be postponed. If you’re arranging to interview someone, you need to check that both you and the contributor are feeling well, if not, it’s not worth the risk of catching it and then spreading it further.
I’ve put our official risk assessment measures for this below, you’re filling out a risk assessment for a shoot, please take these precautions into your assessment.

CORONA RELATED IDEAS
As for ideas, it’s likely that we’ll get a lot of similar proposals for corona related videos.
You’re free to send these over but there will likely be more ideas that we can’t take forward for a variety of reasons. And extra compliance measures will apply.
Also given that most news stories are predominantly related to this, any other type of news and entertainment is welcomed!

We are still definitely open to ideas and if you’re stuck at home then making videos could be a good creative outlet.
Many people may start to film more where they live, I’d ask that you try to get creative where possible for your backdrops and how you use the space for filming otherwise a lot of videos may look the same I.e. Avoid white bedroom walls :)

Hope that all makes sense!

Cheers!

These are the control measures which are the official BBC advice for managing CV risk currently.

 * Wash your hands frequently with soap and water or use a sanitiser gel
 * Catch coughs and sneezes with disposable tissues or clothing, and wash your hands
 * Avoid close contact with people who are unwell
 * Avoid close contact with live or dead farm or wild animals
 * If you are feeling unwell, and/or have any upper respiratory symptoms, you should call NHS 111 (or your local medical provider)

In addition to that I think you should also think about things like

 * Don¹t eat lunch or drink on location without washing hands first
 * Wash hands or use gel after driving a pool car
 * Not shaking hands with contributors (but explaining why ­ protecting both them and us!)

Here is the link for the VC for tomorrow’s meeting for you to distribute to the Convener, Deputy Convener, Members, witnesses and among yourselves.

We would ask that you distribute this later this afternoon or early evening, along with joining instructions (further below) and a request that all VC participants log in half an hour before the meeting starts in public.

Please can you email members these details and embed them in a calendar invitation for the meeting as it makes a significant difference to the workflow.

And when you get a chance, please forward us some indication as to the shape of the meeting – if an order of speakers is available, that would be great, but otherwise, it would make a big difference to get a more general indication on who might be likely to feature when.

It might also be useful for you to provide the following BIT contact information for people who are having problems joining. For this meeting, it should be:

If you need any further information, just drop us a line any time.

JOINING INSTRUCTIONS

You will need Google Chome installed on your machine

 1. Open Google Chrome on your machine

emails.subject: SPPA Committee: Important Information
emails.body:
Hello Jamie

We’re not sure if you have full access to your Scottish Parliament email account so Ruth has asked me to forward SPPA committee information to you as you’ll be covering/shadowing this committee tomorrow.

Standards Committee Thurs 27th Aug 1000-1130hrs
Staff cover: Linnemann P (Peter) Martos J (Juan) Murray J (Jamie)

First-time committee.

Meeting expected to run in public no longer than half an hour.

Agenda attached

Info re RUNNING ORDER:
(1) Meeting will open with Convener inviting a declaration of interest from John Scott
(2) Statement from Minister
(3) Qs from members as follows:

 * Mark Ruskell
 * Maureen Watt
 * Jamie Halcro Johnston
 * Neil Findlay
 * Gil Paterson
 * John Scott
His guidance to members re us is:

 * I’ll invite the questioner to ask their question, then go to the Minister and then come back to the questioner to check whether they have any follow-up questions
 * Once each Member has asked their questions, I’ll move on to the next Member on the list and so on. If your question has already been covered, I would ask you just to say that the matter that you are interested in has already been covered.
 * Interventions and supplementary questions are very difficult for broadcasting to manage so I would discourage you if at all possible from asking them
 * If you absolutely must ask a supplementary, can you please type the letter “R” into the chat function for participants so I can then see that you want in. Please be aware that you will be seen live on camera at all times, even when not speaking. I will take any interventions at the end when everyone has had a chance to ask their questions
 * Please wait until I announce you before speaking
 * Please also be patient and allow our Broadcasting staff a few seconds to turn your microphones on before starting your question
ATTENDING

Clerking Team
Katy Orr
Sam Currie
Joanna Hardy
Alastair Macfie
Members
Bill Kidd
Mark Ruskell
Neil Findlay
Jamie Halcro Johnston
Gil Paterson

Jamie Bowman, Solicitor, Scottish Government Legal Directorate
Al Gibson, Policy Adviser, Parliament and Legislation Unit, Scottish Government
Kenneth Pentland - Senior Policy Officer, Elections Team, Scottish Government
​
BLUE JEANS CODES

Moderator access: https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/eqpybeeb

Presenter access: https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/zydqfbuh

Let me know if you need anything else.

Kind regards
Andrew

Please note that I am currently working from home and can be reached via email & Microsoft teams.

emails.subject: Application for July 2020 Graduation
emails.body:
Application for Summer Graduation
[Edinburgh Napier University]
Dear Jamie Archibald

You will be aware that the University has taken the decision to postpone the summer 2020 graduation ceremonies in light of the current Covid-19 global pandemic.

The University is now providing two options if you are eligible to graduate in July 2020.

You can choose to graduate In Absentia. This would mean that you do not attend a ceremony and you will receive your parchment in the post as soon as is reasonably practical after the publication date of 9 July 2020.

Or you can choose to graduate In Absentia in July 2020 and also indicate that you may wish to attend a future graduation ceremony at a point (yet to be identified) when would be feasible to run these types of events. In this case you would still receive your parchment as soon as is reasonably practical after the July publication date.

Please note that the publication of results date has changed to Thursday 9 July 2020 due to the change in assessment methodology and the impact that this has on subsequent marking and examination board processes.

Please could you now log into eStudent Records and follow the links there for graduation.

The closing date to apply to graduate is Monday 15 June 2020.

If you are an undergraduate student intending to exit with an award in Year 3, and not continue to Honours, please remember to inform your School that you wish to exit so that they can process your award, in addition to completing the application process.

If you have any questions about your graduation, please contact the Graduations team at [email removed]

Yours sincerely

Student Administration

emails.subject: Unlocked [brand new BBC SCOTLAND PODCAST]
emails.body:
Hey,

I know this is a bit of an out of the blue message (and you may not have worked with me on THE SOCIAL in months or ever for that matter) but I just wanted to make you aware of a new BBC Scotland podcast called UNLOCKED. This podcast has been created to give a platform to the issues facing 18-30 year olds in Scotland during this pandemic.

The series aims to focus on an alternative news story each week as well as give breathing space for us to discuss how much our lives have changed. As much as I have been glued to the coronavirus news briefings, I can't help but think there are more stories to be uncovered and I think we need a space to rant about the things that we are struggling with...without feeling guilty because they are not life threatening problems.

These are times like no other and it's normal to be worried sick and frustrated. It's normal to worried about loved ones or get pissed off at a flatmate or rant about how lockdown has impacted a relationship. Even missing gigs, festivals and planned holidays is a huge blow.

Anyway, the purpose of this is to cover stories and, if you are interested in hearing more, here is the link to EPISODE 0 [a placeholder for when new episodes arrive]: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/p08bs8hs

If you want to make sure you don't miss an episode, click SUBSCRIBE on UNLOCKED via BBC Sounds.

This week (Friday), we intend to look at the cancellation of GIGS and FESTIVALS so if you would like to ask a question or put a point to our panel then please send me a voice note with your name, how you feel about events being cancelled and your question.

Thanks for taking the time to read this and please do get in touch if you think there is a subject we should be covering.

Myles

Myles Bonnar
Twitter - @mylesbonnar
Email - [email removed]

Hi Jamie

Great to hear from you and thanks for getting back to me so quickly.

This all sounds great and we would prefer to work around your existing commitments rather than ask you to make any changes with a longer term contract on our behalf.

I think we would be able to make Friday/Mondays work – it all hinges on our dub day which should be a Wednesday. As long as we can get final dubbed versions back in time to get them to you for a Friday (we would taxi them to you on a drive – am I right in saying you are Glasgow based?), we could do that – if that works for you? The series is likely to publish on a Thurs, which makes working on the edits midweek too close to the wire, and it would be easier if you were working on it on days the producer of this show is available to consult with rather than a weekend. Each week will have its own specific set of music rights issues to be dealt with, so it would save time if you are both able to talk about it as you go.

So – could we pencil this with you please? emails.subject: IMPORTANT FILMING GUIDELINES - BBC THE SOCIAL
emails.body:
Hello everyone!

There’s a lot of info below about updating the deliverables and processed for filming, if a big wall of text isn't the easiest way for you to get info, please message me and I can talk through the guidance but keep this email as reference point as well.

Firstly thank you to everyone who’s continued to work away on videos for The Social despite a global pandemic!

As lockdown restrictions have started to ease, there are potentially more viable options for filming outside and with other people, but first and foremost it’s vital you take the necessary precautions to ensure you’re keeping your self and others safe.

The key to this is communication. I’ll set out some general rules below, it won’t cover all situations as the type of content you make is so varied so before you shoot anything you must tell us so we’re not in a position where you’ve made something brilliant but we can’t use it.

No worries. Because of uni getting busy it would probably need to be Tuesday the 18th and Tuesday the 25th as backup if we need more footage. Adult classes are Tuesday 10.30 -11.30am. That ok with you Jamie?

In the mean time I’ll get the hospital script done.

________________________________
From: Ryan Pasi 
Sent: Tuesday, February 4, 2020 11:00:12 AM
To: sanjeev mann ; Jamie Murray 

Hey Sanjeev,

Would defo avoid filming with kids. We need to get consent from all the parents and it’s just a total nightmare.
The Social is aimed at over 18 so generally try to always have ideas and stories based on that so it makes sense for us to highlight the adult sesions.

Are you looking to film this week or next?
Apoligies as I’ve just been catching up with emails today.

Cheers,

Ryan Pasi (he/him)

Content Producer, BBC The Social

0141 422 6974

[thesociallogo]

Facebook | Gaming | YouTube | Instagram | Twitter | bbc.co.uk

From: sanjeev mann >
Date: Sunday, 2 February 2020 at 18:09
To: Jamie Murray >, Ryan Pasi >

Sorry my mistake, the adult classes are on Tuesday and Wednesday from 10.30am to 11.30am. We may need 2 sessions to get everything.

Also Ryan, what's your thoughts on filming with the kids class?

Sent from Samsung Mobile on O2

-------- Original message --------
From: Jamie Murray >
Date: 31/01/2020 12:54 (GMT+00:00)
To: sanjeev mann >

Hey Sanjeev,

Great to hear from you.

Glad to hear you think this idea can work on film.

The Thursday will be the more ideal day for filming as it's probably best to avoid the kids class, given the complications with clearing the filming of all participants - having said that it may still be a possibility. Ryan will definitely no more on that.

So if it is a Thursday the class is on, if you name me a day you'd like to go in the near future my availability is looking pretty open so any day should be fine.

Look forward to hearing from you. Let me know how your phone-call from Ryan goes!

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

Jamie Murray
Videographer
www.jamieamurray.com

On Wednesday, 29 January 2020, 15:40:30 GMT, sanjeev mann > wrote:

Hey Ryan and Jamie,

Yeah i could take part although i am not sure how it would work because of limited movement compared to the rest of the class, although i still think we could do an interesting feature around it. I could still react to the club and give my thoughts on how good a job they’re doing.

Yeah a phone call before sounds good. The class runs every Tuesday and Thursday although Tuesday is a kids class. So would you prefer the Thursday for filming?

Also, Jamie, how soon are you able to come along and help out with filming?

Cheers, Sanjeev.

________________________________

Sent: Wednesday, January 29, 2020 11:56:57 AM

Just introducing you two as I’m keen to get this karate video made.

We should have a quick call prior to shooting and talk through ideas for it too.

I got your contact details from Eileen Irvine at PQ. BBC Arts Digital https://www.bbc.co.uk/arts is running a Live page along with UK Museums sector and I'm looking for, ideally, someone with their own laptop, Premiere and can clip and subtitle films. Best wishes,
Allan.

Best wishes,
Allan.

From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: Thursday, February 18, 2021 10:35:44 AM
To: Strathclyde Musical Theatre Society 

Hi Layla,

That is great that you have found a sound engineer who is now on board.

Great news to hear the job would no longer involve sound mixing, as that isn't something I could offer to a standard that would be required.

With the removal of sound mixing, it is true that would reduce some of the workload. However, the area where there will still be a considerable amount to do will be syncing all of the videos with the master track.

As I mentioned before, for this to be a success, it would mean all of the participants recording their performance with the exact same video settings. Here is some advice as to how to do that:

Everyone should adjust something in their phone settings called the 'video framerate'. On an android: you launch open Camera and jump into Settings > Video Frame Rate and select "30". For an iPhone, open Settings > Camera > Record Video and select > "1080p HD at 30fps". By doing this it will ensure all video files are of the same quality and settings, which should prevent some people's performances from seeming out of sync. It is also important that all videos are filmed in 1080p quality and not 4K, because when editing with both, it can cause disruption and lag, meaning it becomes really difficult to edit. It is also important that everyone uses the same 'base' track when recording their versions. I am glad you like the clap idea! It keeps everyone on track and means everything should be able to be synced properly.

I would also say that 23 songs still does seem a lot, in terms of the editing of this project. As you will know from editing 'Wair For My Shot', it takes a while to sync up all the clips and then the time to carefully place them in a certain order, so there is variety in the performers we see on the screen at any one time. In my experience, it is possible that this may take a few hours of editing for each song. Obviously, some songs will be different with fewer performers etc. In terms of an estimate, with editing priced at £35/hour, it may be anywhere from £840 (going by the estimate of each song only taking an hour) to possibly £1680 or slightly more (if all songs took two hours, but with some likely to take less, this would likely be more accurate of a price estimate, as I am thinking of the additional editing for combining all the songs into one main showpiece clip).

I hope this email gives you a better idea of the filming requirements for a project like this and a better idea of potential costings etc.

I am also happy to speak over Zoom, I am free later in the afternoon next Monday (22nd) if you would still like a zoom call? If that doesn't suit, let me know some other times that you can do and I will get back to you.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

From: Jamie Murray 
Sent: Monday, February 15, 2021 3:43:53 PM
To: Strathclyde Musical Theatre Society 

Hello Charlotte and Layla,

First of all, thank you very much for your email.

Thank you for providing the details to the extent which you have, it is really helpful for me to get an idea of exactly what you are looking for.

The main point for me that I would like to stress is that I don't have a background in sound mixing/design and if that forms a big part of what you require, I wouldn't be able to offer anything more, in terms of the quality of the vocal arrangements and sound quality, of the video - Wait For My Shot - that you already sent across, unfortunately.

Recently, I did work with a client where I edited together a large number of instruments and combined all the performances. The syncing of clips and general editing, which would be similar to the 'Wait For My Shot' video, did take a long time and that was just for one song. Therefore, if you are looking for 23 songs to be individually edited and then combined all together in a showcase video, my concern would be that it would take a very long time to edit. As can be seen from my website, my hourly rate for video editing is £35 per hour - so given the amount of time that would need to be spent editing all the videos, it would be a large estimate for this project as each song may take a few hours each to edit, especially the songs with various musicians/vocalists. Also, I am very aware of how difficult funding and fundraising is for a university group. I wouldn't want to quote a large, unrealistic price. Would there be any alternatives, such as limiting the number of songs in the showpiece or alternatively, once the restrictions ease, we could look into recording a performance? That may be more visually interesting for viewers rather than a home recording? I may be wrong here or indeed it may not be what you are looking for. but I would love to hear your thoughts. I would be happy to look into the possibility of shooting a music video type project; if that were an area you would like to explore.

Another issue that I think would be relevant to make you aware of is the need for all the musicians and vocalists to be filming with the exact same settings on their phone/camera, as I ran into various problems of having different frame rates which meant some performances could never line up with the rest of the group. Also, there needs to be a part of the backing track at the start where it counts down from 3,2,1 and then everyone claps at the same time because trying to sync up the same tracks without an audible reference point to go from can prove to be very difficult.

I have tried to give an overview of the problems I have run into with similar projects in the past, as it may give you an indication of where you want to go moving forward. Hopefully, we can work towards something together as it would be great to be involved in something like this.

I look forward to hearing from you and thanks once again for your email.

Have a lovely week.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

Hi Layla,

That is great that you have found a sound engineer who is now on board.

Great news to hear the job would no longer involve sound mixing, as that isn't something I could offer to a standard that would be required.

With the removal of sound mixing, it is true that would reduce some of the workload. However, the area where there will still be a considerable amount to do will be syncing all of the videos with the master track.

As I mentioned before, for this to be a success, it would mean all of the participants recording their performance with the exact same video settings. Here is some advice as to how to do that:

Everyone should adjust something in their phone settings called the 'video framerate'. On an android: you launch open Camera and jump into Settings > Video Frame Rate and select "30". For an iPhone, open Settings > Camera > Record Video and select > "1080p HD at 30fps". By doing this it will ensure all video files are of the same quality and settings, which should prevent some people's performances from seeming out of sync. It is also important that all videos are filmed in 1080p quality and not 4K, because when editing with both, it can cause disruption and lag, meaning it becomes really difficult to edit. It is also important that everyone uses the same 'base' track when recording their versions. I am glad you like the clap idea! It keeps everyone on track and means everything should be able to be synced properly.

I would also say that 23 songs still does seem a lot, in terms of the editing of this project. As you will know from editing 'Wair For My Shot', it takes a while to sync up all the clips and then the time to carefully place them in a certain order, so there is variety in the performers we see on the screen at any one time. In my experience, it is possible that this may take a few hours of editing for each song. Obviously, some songs will be different with fewer performers etc. In terms of an estimate, with editing priced at £35/hour, it may be anywhere from £840 (going by the estimate of each song only taking an hour) to possibly £1680 or slightly more (if all songs took two hours, but with some likely to take less, this would likely be more accurate of a price estimate, as I am thinking of the additional editing for combining all the songs into one main showpiece clip).

I hope this email gives you a better idea of the filming requirements for a project like this and a better idea of potential costings etc.

I am also happy to speak over Zoom, I am free later in the afternoon next Monday (22nd) if you would still like a zoom call? If that doesn't suit, let me know some other times that you can do and I will get back to you.

Kindest of regards,

Hello Jamie!

My god you work fast lol that turn around was crazy!! Genuinely can't stop watching the video lol it looks great!!

We have a couple of notes though:

 * would it be possible to get rid of the black lines in between the videos? if not, would it be possible to make these as thin as they could possibly be please?
 * When it is the 3 principle girls on the screen, is there any way to zoom them out just a wee bit to see a little bit more of their arm choreography?
 * and at the end (2:40) when they all throw their hands up in the air, can Carolyn (principle Jenna with blonde hair) be in the middle of the three principle girls please?

Apart from those wee things we already absolutely adore the video!!

I want to apologise for the different frame rates for their videos, we have put up a video explaining them, they have a pdf booklet explaining how to film their videos and they are reminded every week so I am not sure how else we can annoy them with it lol. However, we will be putting out more reminders and we will resend the pdf to everyone to ensure that they definitely know that they need to film in these frame rates. Unfortunately, though in terms of videos for the first act of the showcase we basically have them all in, we are only waiting for 1-2 videos for around 8 of the first act songs so if these videos are different frame rates it's very likely that these songs will have that too. So, I am glad that for this song it didn't cause too much bother and hopefully it stays like that for the rest of act one and then everyone will actually listen to us for act two.

Again, apologies for the time stamps, when we made the video profiles, we went off of our rehearsal track time stamps and forgot to update them with Cheryl's draft time stamps so I will get that sorted for the rest of them before we send them to you.

Looking forward to seeing the next edit of the video!!

Best wishes,
Charlotte

On Wednesday, 31 March 2021, 12:14:44 BST, Jamie Murray wrote:

Hello Charlotte,

Thank you very much for all of this.

I have downloaded all the material from Google Drive and the video editing profile appears to be very helpful, so thank you very much for that.

A few things I have noticed just from looking at the videos and music overall; the first being that most of the videos are all at different framerates. As you will remember, I had stressed the importance of everyone filming in the same framerate during our chat and in the emails. Layla had emailed me in February saying you both would be able to provide a tutorial for members on how to set both apple and android phones to the correct video settings. I wondered if you both had managed to do this? If not, it would be great to get everyone onto the same settings for everything else that is going to be filmed in future. The issue with differing framerates means that essentially after I have synced each clip up with the clap at the beginning, as the video goes on some of them appear out of time with the music and can make the editing process much more complicated and in some cases, it may mean that certain people can't be shown. Also, I noticed that one of the band members didn't do a clap at the beginning, which again makes it all the more difficult to sync up with everyone else. PLEASE don't worry about this too much at the minute for this video just yet, as I am yet to try editing it all together and afterwards, I will have a better idea of any issues. But for the future, we do need everyone to be using the same settings and clapping at the exact same time.

Hopefully, I can work around this for the first song, but if I have any issues I will let you know. If you need assistance on how to get everyone to film on the same framerates/settings then please let me know, and I will source or make some tutorial videos to help with that.

Thanks for all your help so far, I am looking forward to beginning the edit.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Broadway's Best: An Online Showcase
emails.body:
Hey Jamie,

Following your email the other day, I had a bit of a raid through my contacts and managed to get in touch with a sound engineer called Cheryl who I had previously worked with on a few projects at Glasgow music studios and have managed to get her on board. Cheryl will be combining all of the vocal and instrumental tracks, cleaning and balancing them, and mixing them down into a single audio track.

This would then change what we had originally asked you to do as the job would no longer involve any kind of sound mixing. We would just need you to combine everyone's videos for each individual song in a presentable way, remove the audios from the videos and then sync them with them with the new audio track that will be mixed by Cheryl for each song. Then we would want you to combine all the individual songs into one large video so we would be able to stream it in one go as a ticketed event.

We would still very much like to have a zoom meeting with you to discuss the logistics of the project and nail down the potential costings etc. But hopefully by removing the sound mixing from the job, your workload would be reduced considerably.

Looking forward to hearing from you,
Layla 😊

P.S. the '1,2,3, clap' thing is an excellent idea and would have made my life a million times easier when I was editing 'Wait For My Shot' ahahaaa

emails.subject: SHOUT-OUT: Post-Lockdown Anxiety [BBC The Social]
emails.body:
This shoutout has a deadline of 1600, 23rd February (today)

Hi,

I hope you don't mind receiving an email on the subject of anxiety but we felt this would be the quickest way to ask our contributors about an important, timely subject.

Today, FM Nicola Sturgeon will likely announce Scotland's roadmap to restriction-easing as we tackle the coronavirus pandemic (nearly a year on from Lockdown 1). As part of the prospect of coming out of lockdown, we have been hearing that some people are feeling anxious about the prospect of society opening back up. BBC The Social, as a platform, takes mental health extremely seriously and we felt it was important that we cover this subject with care, inviting a trained medical professional to offer advice in a video and article format.

However, we feel it is important to hear from young adults about so-called 'post-lockdown anxiety' and I am keen to hear from anyone about their experience of this.

So, if you have been experiencing increased anxiety from the notion of society returning to "normal", can you respond with the following details:

 * Name: [we will likely only use your first name]
 * Age:
 * Location (Central belt, Highlands etc etc):
 * How has the prospect of lockdown-easing impacted you? (max 150 words):
 * What are your main concerns if/when lockdown is lifted? (max 150 words):
 * What has helped you when you have become anxious? (max 150 words):
 * Please also attach a picture (
07716092331

Hello Charlotte,

My day yesterday was less busy and I have a few busy days coming up so I wanted to get ahead with the first video as soon as possible. Glad you enjoy and are happy with the video so far.

In terms of the changes;
• the black lines are there as a result of the grids I made, which I talked about on our zoom call. I created a preset of various transparent images which mirrored the layout you had drawn in the video profile and worked from those. The videos of the band and vocalists were then all cropped to fit that exact size, so it might be very difficult to take away the black bars now as that will mean having to resize every clip for every different layout. Moving forward though, I will ensure that the new preset images I create will have thin lines, to maximise the space on the screen. Hope that is okay?

• Unfortunately, because I have had to cropped the videos for them to fit in the layout with every other video, I already have used as much of the video as I can. The difficulty with this is caused when people move around the frame when filming, it can be difficult to track that for everyone during the edit, as it isn't easy to have the clip move around within the square/section it is playing, otherwise we would end up losing the top or bottom of the image. I will take a look and try as best I can to adjust where possible.

• Yes no problem, I will have that changed for you in the next edit.

Glad we are off to a great start, albeit with a few changes needed here and there.

That is unfortunate about the video framerates as you know how much I stressed that point. Just because of a previous experience it caused great issues. However, it has gone well this time so as long as everyone sticks to the method they used for filming the first video, we should be fine!!!

That is great about the timestamps, it just means I can change things exact to the second you would like. Thanks very much for that.

I will get to work on trying to improve the video soon and I will be back in touch soon.

Kind regards,
Jamie

emails.subject: Visit Bute video work
emails.body:
Hi Jamie,

Im one of the directors of Visit Bute and we have recently been awarded a bit of funding to do some video work to promote the island to tourists.

One of my very god friends Lorna happens to be a lecturer at city of Glasgow college and highly recommend you, and when i mentioned you in our last board meeting Laura who’s is our marketing whizz said you were related!

Today, FM Nicola Sturgeon will likely announce Scotland's roadmap to restriction-easing as we tackle the coronavirus pandemic (nearly a year on from Lockdown 1). emails.subject: Graduation Update
emails.body:
[Graduates 2020]

Dear Jamie,

Graduation is the culmination of your hard work and celebrating your success is a highlight for everyone at the University.

As you know, the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic meant we were unable to hold ceremonies in July or October last year. At the time, we hoped that we would be back to normal by our 2021 ceremonies.

Unfortunately, due to ongoing uncertainty caused by the pandemic we will be unable to host our usual ceremonies in the Usher Hall in July 2021 either. Although there has been positive news from the Scottish Government recently around opening up more of society, it is very unlikely that mass gatherings on this scale will be allowed as early as July.

Like other universities across Scotland, we have therefore made the difficult decision to cancel our ceremonies. It also means that we cannot have the class of 2020 back to celebrate in person as we had hoped.

We know that this will be disappointing news as you indicated that you would be keen to return for a graduation ceremony. However, just because we cannot host a ceremony does not mean that we cannot celebrate your achievements.

We appreciate that you had to adapt to complete your education. Things changed. The world is different. With that in mind, how we will now celebrate your graduation will also be different.

We want the world to know how proud we are of you. We want to shout about your success. We want to get your name out there.

So, while we cannot get you up onto the Usher Hall stage, we will be celebrating in style this July and we will let you know the full details nearer the time. We don’t want to say too much at this point and ruin the surprise, but suffice to say, your name will most definitely be out there. We’re excited!

On a practical level, what does this mean? To be involved, you need to give us consent to include your name in the virtual celebration and to be displayed in public in Edinburgh. You can tell us if you would like to be involved by clicking on this link and indicating your preference in the survey.

If you do not reply by April 9, 2021 we will assume that you do not want to be involved and your name will not be included. Regretfully no late submission of names will be accepted after this date.

Beyond this summer, when restrictions are lifted, we hope to give you the opportunity for photographs on campus and for a class of 2020 reunion where you will be able to celebrate with your classmates.

There is hope on the horizon. It may have come too late for your graduation ceremony but the spirit of graduations lives on at Edinburgh Napier. We look forward to marking your special moment in a manner that befits the huge efforts you have made to gain your degree.

We’ll be in touch again soon.

Regards

The Graduations Team

featured.to: Matt Pinder [private email - not for sharing]
featured.subject: Student in search of advice!
featured.body:
Dear Matt,

My name is Jamie Murray, a fourth year television student studying in Glasgow. Thank you for passing your email on to my lecturer Kate Cotter. I really appreciate it.

I was very taken aback by your documentary on the Margaret Fleming murder trial. I am originally from the Isle of Bute and therefore I am used to driving past the house where Margaret had lived. I remember very clearly people talking about the case when the news first broke and I felt your documentary done an incredible job at highlighting the failures in the system whereby a vulnerable person can simply be forgotten about. It is a very tragic story but one that is definitely worth being told. Having cameras in the court room was a really great insight into that world also and something I have never really seen before. Very informative!

I'd love to meet with you to get your advice on career progression, the pathway that you have taken and just general tips for moving forward once I complete my education. I have been very lucky to receive a short-term freelance opportunity whilst I finish my degree and that begins next week. So, would you be available at some point this week to meet with me?

I understand you will be very busy, Kate had mentioned about being in an edit for another project, so I don't want to get in your way at all or keep you long. It would just be very beneficial to meet you.

Look forward to hearing from you.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie Murray
Videographer
www.jamieamurray.com

---

Matt replied the same afternoon offering coffee the next day or Friday. They met in Glasgow that week. Matt later offered Jamie the opportunity to sit in on an edit.

featured.subject: Work Experience / Meeting Request — Stephen Bennett
featured.body:
Dear Stephen,

My name is Jamie Murray. I am currently a 4th year TV student at City of Glasgow College. After discussing with my lecturer, Kate Cotter, about my interest in production and career aspirations she advised me to get in contact with you.

After I delved deeper I realised that your productions have actually had a massive impact on me. I really admire the access you manage to get in your documentaries and the areas of life which you successfully showcase. There are a few of your recent projects which I particularly enjoyed.

I am from and was born on the Isle of Bute, which forms part of the Argyll & Bute local authority. Therefore, I took great interest in The Country Council. I am a former elected member of the Scottish Youth Parliament having represented Argyll & Bute from 2015 until 2019, and your programme really focused on the hardships the council and council workers are now facing and how that impacts the people of Argyll & Bute. I am interested in the logistics challenges you faced when filming that series. I was also fascinated to hear, from Kate, that you completely self-shot that and do so for the majority of your projects. That is extremely impressive.

Another one of your productions I thought was extremely thought-provoking and insightful was Dunblane: Our Story that I seen on BBC 1 Scotland. It is no surprise that you won the BAFTA for Best Single Doc. I wonder how you approach such a tragic issue and how you crafted such a compelling narrative out of what was such an awful event?

I look forward to checking out Pride and Privilege. As I mentioned I am interested in politics and social and class division in Scottish society so this show seems right up my street.

I wanted to get in contact with you to see if there was any chance you allow students to shadow you in a production to learn from your methods? Or if you are too busy to accommodate another person on shoot, if we could meet for a coffee? I would be fascinated to learn more about what inspires you and the path you took which led you to where you are now.

I have attached my CV and here is a link to my showreel: https://www.jamieamurray.com/showreel. If you have any spare time I would really appreciate any advice on either my CV or Showreel.

Have a wonderful weekend and I look forward to hearing from you.

Kindest of regards,
Jamie Murray

---

Stephen Bennett replied the same day:

"Hey Jamie — Thanks for all this, and say hi to Kate. This is a great letter. Actually one of the best I have received about such requests. Its equally great that you have your website and so people can get a real sense of you. Well done on both accounts. I'm in the edit now so there are no opportunities for shadowing and my next project is very sensitive so won't be possible — so lets meet up."

They met for coffee in Glasgow city centre the following month.

featured.subject: SSSA Film Director Application 2020
featured.body:
Hello,

My name is Jamie Murray and I am applying for the exciting role of Film Director for the Scottish Social Services Awards 2020, following my rewarding experience of taking part last year. I'm currently a fourth-year BA Hons student at City of Glasgow College studying Television Production.

Since taking part in the SSSA in 2019 (for which, I directed two films: #SSSA19 Category 5: Shelter Scotland and #SSSA19 Category 4: Dundee City Council and Partners) I have filmed a number of other projects of a similar nature. During the summer, I was commissioned to create a one minute video for the Scottish Parliament focussed on a Syrian refugee called Mounzer: https://youtu.be/ru_LITxyt5M.

Additionally, I have filmed and edited various short form videos for the Rangers Charity Foundation: Everyone Anyone: VI Football, Glen Kamara launches new Foundation partnership and Rangers Charity Foundation Dream Day.

Furthermore, I also create videos for BBC The Social that can all be found here: BBC | Jamie Murray. Since I directed two videos last year for the SSSA, I have undertaken many projects of a similar nature and tackled various difficult topics such as death, disabilities and injustice. I believe these experiences make me a great candidate who can be trusted to take sensitive subject matter and create interesting impactful films, worthy of being shown at the SSSA in 2020.

I hope to be considered for this rewarding opportunity to again make videos for a very worthwhile cause. I am also on track with my coursework and can provide the contact details of my lecturer, Kate Cotter, to confirm this.

I have attached my CV below as requested.

Yours faithfully,
Jamie Murray
Videographer
www.jamieamurray.com

---

Lorna Saunders (Pagoda PR) replied within 30 minutes: "Thanks Jamie. Nice to hear from you again. I'll be back in touch after the deadline for applications." Jamie was awarded the role.

featured.subject: A professional asking a student for camera advice
featured.body:
Stephen Bennett (Producer/Director, Dunblane: Our Story) emailed Jamie — a student — to ask for advice on autofocus settings for the Sony A7III. Stephen had just bought the same camera Jamie was using.

Stephen asked:

"Hi Jamie — Can I ask a quick favour: What are your best A7iii settings for autofocus on your gimbal. For people and GVs. Having been a Panasonic guy for so long I'm still trying to get my head around the new camera."

Jamie replied with detailed menu settings across two camera menus, explaining when to switch between modes depending on what was being shot.

Stephen replied: "fab, thanks Jamie - I have got all these settings the same, so that's encouraging. Lovely bit of kit."

---

This exchange shows what networking can lead to beyond the initial meeting. An award-winning documentary filmmaker came back to a student for technical advice — because Jamie had built a genuine professional relationship, demonstrated real knowledge, and made himself useful. The relationship was two-way.
